title: Rendang Recipe: Authentic Minangkabau Beef Rendang
description: A rich and spicy beef dish slow-cooked in coconut milk and a blend of aromatic spices. Originally from Minangkabau, West Sumatra, rendang is often served at special occasions and celebrations.
ingredients: 1 kg beef tenderloin, cut into 4 cm pieces
2 liters thick coconut milk from 3 coconuts
3 cm ginger, 3 cm turmeric, 3 cm galangal
instructions: Toast the ground spice paste without oil until fragrant and moisture reduces, about 10 minutes.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaves. Stir well.
Pour coconut milk into a large wok, add the toasted spices and beef. Stir well.
Bring to a boil over high heat while stirring, then reduce to low heat.
Cook on low heat for 3-4 hours, stirring occasionally. The coconut milk will reduce and release oil.
Once thickened and oily, add salt and palm sugar. Stir well.
Cook while stirring more frequently to prevent burning, until the sauce is nearly dry and the meat turns dark brownish-black.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Soto Betawi Recipe: Authentic Jakarta Beef Soup
description: A rich and creamy beef soup from Jakarta, featuring tender chunks of beef in a coconut milk-based broth with aromatic spices.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 candlenuts, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp coriander
Garnish: fried potatoes, tomatoes, spring onions, fried shallots, melinjo crackers, lime, chili sambal
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Remove and dice. Reserve the broth.
Grind all spice paste ingredients. Sauté in oil until fragrant.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Sauté until wilted.
Pour in beef broth and coconut milk. Stir well. Add the beef.
Cook over medium heat until boiling, then pour in the milk.
Stir gently so the coconut milk and milk don't curdle.
Add salt, sugar, and bouillon powder. Adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with fried potatoes, tomatoes, spring onions, fried shallots, melinjo crackers, and lime.

title: Rawon Recipe: East Java Black Beef Soup
description: A beef soup from East Java with a deep black broth from kluwek nuts. Has a savory and slightly bitter flavor. Served with salted eggs and short bean sprouts.
ingredients: 500 g beef tenderloin, cut into 3 cm pieces
Salt, sugar, bouillon powder to taste
Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 4 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 3 candlenuts, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper
Garnish: short bean sprouts, salted eggs, chili sambal, prawn crackers, fried shallots
instructions: Boil beef in 1.5 liters of water until tender. Remove beef, strain the broth. Dice the beef.
Soak kluwek flesh in hot water, then grind into a black paste.
Sauté the spice paste with the kluwek paste until fragrant.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Stir until wilted.
Pour the sautéed spices into the beef broth. Stir well.
Add the beef. Cook on low heat until spices are absorbed.
Add salt, sugar, and bouillon powder. Adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with rice, short bean sprouts, salted eggs, chili sambal, and prawn crackers.

title: Pempek Recipe: Authentic Palembang Fish Cake
description: A savory fish cake delicacy from Palembang, South Sumatra, served with a sweet and sour vinegar sauce called cuko.
ingredients: Cuko sauce: 250 g palm sugar, 500 ml water, 10 bird's eye chilies, 5 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tsp salt
Garnish: yellow noodles, cucumber, dried shrimp powder
instructions: Mix ground mackerel with garlic, salt, sugar, and egg. Stir well.
Add ice water gradually while mixing until the dough is smooth.
Add sago flour gradually while kneading until shapeable.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add a little oil.
Shape dough as desired (round, long, or submarine with egg filling).
Boil pempek until they float (10-15 minutes). Remove and drain.
Deep fry briefly before serving for a crispy exterior (optional).
Cuko: Boil palm sugar with water until dissolved. Grind chilies and garlic, add to sugar mixture. Add tamarind paste and salt.

title: Gudeg Recipe: Authentic Yogyakarta Jackfruit Stew
description: A sweet dish from Yogyakarta made from young jackfruit cooked with coconut milk and palm sugar for hours. Served with chicken opor, pindang eggs, and krecek crackers.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 4 candlenuts, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper
Garnish: chicken opor, pindang eggs, krecek, steamed rice
instructions: Boil young jackfruit in water for 15 minutes. Discard water. Repeat once. Drain.
Sauté ground spice paste until fragrant. Add bay leaves, galangal, and lemongrass.
Add young jackfruit, stir well with the spices.
Pour in coconut milk and add shredded palm sugar. Stir well.
Cook on low heat for 3-4 hours until jackfruit is tender and sauce thickens.
Stir occasionally to prevent burning at the bottom.
Add salt. Adjust seasoning — gudeg is known for its sweet, rich flavor.
Serve with chicken opor, pindang eggs, krecek, and warm steamed rice.

title: Coto Makassar
description: A rich, peanut-based beef soup from Makassar, South Sulawesi, served with ketupat rice cakes and lime.
ingredients: Salt and beef bouillon powder to taste
Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper, 3 candlenuts
Garnish: rice cakes, spring onions, lime, chili sambal, fried shallots
instructions: Boil beef in 1.5 liters of water until tender. Remove beef, dice. Strain the broth.
Grind roasted peanuts with a little water into a paste.
Sauté ground spice paste in oil until fragrant. Add lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Pour beef broth into the sautéed spices. Add peanut paste. Stir well.
Cook on low heat until broth thickens and becomes oily, about 30 minutes.
Add diced beef. Add salt and bouillon powder.
Cook until broth is very thick and spices are fully absorbed.
Serve hot with rice cakes, spring onions, fried shallots, and lime.

title: Ayam Taliwang Recipe: Spicy Lombok Grilled Chicken
description: A spicy grilled chicken dish from Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara, marinated in a fiery chili paste.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 15 red chilies, 10 bird's eye chilies, 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 2 cm kencur, 2 candlenuts, 1 tsp roasted shrimp paste, 1 tomato
instructions: Grind all spice paste ingredients. Sauté in oil until fragrant and cooked.
Add kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass. Stir well.
Pour in coconut milk, tamarind water, salt, and palm sugar. Bring to a boil.
Add chicken, coat well with the sauce. Cook on low heat until sauce is absorbed and thickened.
Heat the grill. Grill chicken while basting with remaining sauce until golden brown.
Flip the chicken and baste again. Grill the other side until cooked.
Serve with warm rice and plecing kangkung (water spinach).

title: Papeda Recipe: Eastern Indonesia Sago Porridge
description: A staple food from Papua and Maluku made from sago starch, served with a yellow turmeric-spiced broth and fish. A unique and healthy alternative to rice.
ingredients: Yellow broth: 500 g tuna, 1 liter water, 3 tbsp oil
3 cm roasted turmeric, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves
2 cm ginger, 3 kaffir lime leaves, 2 lemongrass stalks
1 green tomato, whole bird's eye chilies
Salt, bouillon powder, 1 tbsp lime juice
Garnish: papaya leaf greens, dabu-dabu chili sambal
instructions: Bring water with salt to a boil. Reduce heat.
Sprinkle sago flour gradually while stirring quickly until it clumps and thickens.
Keep stirring until sago is cooked and has a sticky, elastic texture. Set aside.
Sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add ground turmeric, ginger, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass. Sauté until wilted.
Pour in water. Bring to a boil. Add fish and whole bird's eye chilies.
Add salt and bouillon powder. Cook until fish is done.
Serve papeda with the yellow fish broth and dabu-dabu sambal.

title: Sate Madura Recipe: Authentic Madura Chicken Satay
description: Juicy chicken skewers grilled over charcoal, served with a rich peanut sauce and rice cakes.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: 250 g roasted peanuts, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp tamarind water, 200 ml water, 3 tbsp sweet soy sauce
Marinade: 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tbsp sweet soy sauce, 1 tsp salt
Garnish: rice cakes, sliced shallots, chili sambal, sweet soy sauce
instructions: Marinate chicken with the marinade ingredients. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Thread chicken onto bamboo skewers, 4-5 pieces per skewer.
Grind roasted peanuts, shallots, chilies, and palm sugar.
Cook peanut sauce with water, add salt and tamarind water. Simmer until thickened. Add sweet soy sauce.
Grill satay over charcoal or grill. Flip and baste with peanut sauce.
Grill until cooked and slightly charred.
Serve with peanut sauce, rice cakes, sliced shallots, and chili sambal.

title: Mie Aceh Recipe: Spicy Aceh Noodles
description: Spicy stir-fried noodles from Aceh, featuring a bold blend of chili, cumin, and curry spices with tender beef or seafood.
ingredients: 2 tbsp sweet soy sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce

Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 10 bird's eye chilies, 3 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp black pepper, 2 cardamom pods, 1 tsp curry powder
Garnish: melinjo crackers, carrot-cucumber pickle, fried shallots
instructions: Rinse noodles with hot water, drain. Toss with a little oil to prevent sticking.
Sauté ground spice paste in oil until fragrant and cooked.
Add lamb/beef, cook until color changes and meat is done.
Add noodles. Stir well with the spices.
Add sweet soy sauce, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cook while stirring until spices are evenly distributed.
Add sliced spring onions. Stir briefly.
Serve hot with fried shallots, melinjo crackers, and pickle.

title: Original Betawi Soto
description: The authentic Betawi soto with a clear, turmeric-infused broth and tender beef pieces.
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Cut into cubes.
Make broth with turmeric and aromatics.
Add beef and simmer.
Serve with fried potatoes, tomatoes, and emping.
Add lime and sambal to taste.

title: Javanese Fried Rice
description: Authentic Javanese nasi goreng with sweet soy sauce, shrimp paste, and aromatic spices from Central Java.
instructions: Heat oil in wok over high heat.
Fry eggs, scramble and set aside.
Stir-fry shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add terasi, stir until fragrant.
Add rice, kecap manis, and chilies.
Toss well with high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Add scrambled eggs back, mix well.
Serve with cucumber slices and kerupuk.

title: Rica-Rica Grilled Chicken
description: Fiery North Sulawesi grilled chicken with a bold chili-based rica-rica paste.
ingredients: Rica paste: 15 red chilies, 8 shallots, 4 garlic, ginger, lemongrass
instructions: Grind rica paste ingredients.
Marinate chicken with paste.
Grill over charcoal for 25 minutes.
Baste frequently.
Serve with lime and rice.

title: Lamongan Soto
description: Authentic Lamongan soto with koya, shredded chicken, and clear turmeric broth.
ingredients: Koya: crushed prawn crackers and fried garlic
instructions: Boil chicken until tender. Shred the meat.
Make broth with turmeric and spices.
Serve with glass noodles, cabbage, shredded chicken, and egg.
Top with koya.
Add lime and sambal to taste.

title: Smoky Grilled Rib Soup
description: Beef ribs grilled first for smoky flavor, then simmered into rich soup.
ingredients: Spice paste: shallots, garlic, ginger, coriander, pepper
instructions: Season and grill ribs until charred.
Boil grilled ribs for 2 hours until tender.
Add spice paste to broth.
Add vegetables and simmer.
Serve with rice and fried shallots.

title: Steamed Bolu Cake
description: Soft steamed sponge cakes that bloom open like flowers.
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until fluffy.
Add flour, coconut milk, baking powder, and baking soda.
Mix until smooth.
Pour into molds (3/4 full).
Steam for 15-20 minutes on high heat.
Cakes should bloom open like flowers.

title: Goat Fried Rice
description: Bold, gamey fried rice with tender goat meat and aromatic spices.
instructions: Sauté goat meat with garlic and spices until browned.
Add onions and cook until soft.
Push to the side, scramble eggs.
Add rice and sweet soy sauce.
Toss until everything is well combined.

title: Coconut Soup Ice
description: Refreshing young coconut flesh in sweet coconut water with ice.
instructions: Open coconuts and pour water into glasses.
Scrape flesh and add to glasses.
Add crushed ice.
Drizzle with condensed milk and sugar syrup.
Stir and enjoy.

title: Fragrant Grilled Chicken
description: Grilled chicken infused with pandan, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves.
ingredients: Aromatic paste: shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, lemongrass, pandan, kaffir lime leaves, coriander
instructions: Grind aromatic paste ingredients.
Marinate chicken with paste and coconut milk.
Let sit for 2 hours.
Grill over charcoal, basting with sweet soy sauce.
The pandan and lime leaves create incredible aroma.

title: Authentic Lamongan Soto
description: Real Lamongan soto with koya, shredded chicken, and clear turmeric broth.
ingredients: Koya: crushed prawn crackers and fried garlic
instructions: Boil chicken until tender. Shred the meat.
Make broth with turmeric and spices.
Serve with glass noodles, cabbage, shredded chicken, and egg.
Top with koya (crushed crackers and garlic).
Add lime and sambal to taste.

title: Tahu Tek
description: Surabaya street food — fried tofu and rice cake drenched in spicy peanut sauce.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: roasted peanuts, red chilies, garlic, sweet soy sauce, lime juice, salt, water
instructions: Arrange tofu, rice cake cubes, and bean sprouts on a plate.
Grind peanuts, chilies, and garlic into a sauce.
Add sweet soy sauce, lime juice, salt, and water.
Pour sauce over the ingredients.
Drizzle with extra sweet soy sauce and fried shallots.

title: Banjar Chicken Soup
description: Fragrant chicken soup from South Kalimantan with cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 4 garlic cloves, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander
Hard-boiled eggs, potato cakes, rice vermicelli
instructions: Boil chicken with water, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, lemongrass, and lime leaves.
Sauté ground spice paste until fragrant and add to broth.
Cook until chicken is tender. Remove and shred.
Serve broth with shredded chicken, hard-boiled eggs, potato cakes, and rice vermicelli.

title: Seafood Fried Noodles
description: Indonesian fried noodles loaded with shrimp, squid, and fish cakes.
instructions: Cook noodles until al dente. Drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry garlic until fragrant. Add shrimp and squid.
Push to the side, scramble eggs.
Add vegetables and stir-fry until wilted.
Add noodles, sweet soy sauce, and soy sauce.
Toss everything together until well combined. Serve hot.

title: Crispy Tempeh Fritters
description: Golden, crispy tempeh coated in a spiced flour batter.
instructions: Slice tempeh into thin pieces.
Mix rice flour, all-purpose flour, coriander, garlic powder, salt, and water into a batter.
Dip tempeh slices into batter.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with chili sauce.

title: Shaken Avocado Ice
description: Creamy iced drink with fresh avocado, condensed milk, and chocolate syrup.
instructions: Scoop avocado flesh into a glass.
Add crushed ice until the glass is full.
Drizzle generously with sweetened condensed milk.
Add chocolate syrup on top.
Stir and enjoy immediately.

title: Seafood Fried Rice
description: Luxurious fried rice with shrimp, squid, and fish cakes.
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over very high heat.
Stir-fry garlic until fragrant.
Add seafood and cook for 2 minutes.
Push to the side, scramble eggs.
Add rice and break up any clumps.
Add sweet soy sauce, pepper, and vegetables.
Toss everything together until heated through.

title: Savory Egg Martabak
description: Crispy, stuffed pancake filled with spiced egg and meat mixture.
ingredients: Dough: 300 g flour, 1 egg, 1 tsp salt, 150 ml water, oil
Filling: 4 eggs, 200 g minced meat, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 5 green chilies, salt, pepper
Pickled cucumber and chili vinegar for serving
instructions: Make dough: mix flour, egg, salt, and water. Knead until smooth. Rest for 1 hour.
Filling: mix eggs, minced meat, chopped shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Divide dough into balls. Stretch paper-thin on an oiled surface.
Place filling in the center and fold into a square packet.
Fry in a flat pan with oil until golden and crispy on both sides.
Cut into pieces and serve with pickles.

title: Honey Grilled Chicken
description: Succulent chicken marinated in honey-soy glaze, grilled until caramelized.
instructions: Mix honey, sweet soy sauce, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Marinate chicken for 2 hours or overnight.
Grill over medium heat, basting with marinade.
Cook for 20-25 minutes, turning frequently.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Meatballs
description: Bouncy chicken meatballs in clear aromatic broth.
ingredients: Broth: chicken stock, garlic, spring onions, celery
instructions: Mix ground chicken, tapioca, egg whites, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Add ice water gradually and knead until smooth and bouncy.
Shape into balls.
Boil in water until they float.
Soak in ice water to firm up.
Prepare clear broth. Serve meatballs in broth with noodles and condiments.

title: Balinese Fish Satay
description: Traditional minced fish satay wrapped around lemongrass stalks.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, kencur, turmeric, and coriander into a paste.
Mix fish mince with spice paste, toasted coconut, and salt.
Take portions and wrap around lemongrass stalks.
Grill over charcoal for 5-7 minutes, turning frequently.
Serve with sambal matah and steamed rice.

title: Balinese Mixed Vegetable Salad
description: Balinese gado-gado with blanched vegetables, tofu, tempeh, and rich peanut sauce.
ingredients: Mixed vegetables: long beans, bean sprouts, cabbage, spinach
Peanut sauce: roasted peanuts, red chilies, garlic, sweet soy sauce, lime juice, tamarind water, salt
instructions: Blanch vegetables until just tender. Drain.
Fry tofu and tempeh until golden.
Grind peanut sauce ingredients until thick.
Arrange vegetables, tofu, tempeh, and egg on a plate.
Pour peanut sauce generously over everything.
Serve with prawn crackers.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung: Village Fried Rice Recipe
shortTitle: Nasi Goreng Kampung: Village Fried Rice Recipe
description: Rustic homestyle fried rice with anchovies, peanuts, and chili.
instructions: Fry anchovies until crispy. Set aside.
Stir-fry garlic and belacan until fragrant.
Add rice and sweet soy sauce. Toss well.
Add chilies and peanuts.
Serve topped with crispy anchovies, sliced cucumber, and a fried egg.

title: Smashed Fried Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken smashed and served with fiery sambal.
ingredients: Spice paste for boiling: garlic, turmeric, coriander, salt
Flour coating: 100 g flour, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp pepper, salt
Sambal: 15 red chilies, 5 garlic cloves, 1 tsp shrimp paste, salt, lime juice
instructions: Boil chicken with spice paste until almost cooked.
Drain and coat with seasoned flour.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Make sambal by grinding chilies, garlic, and shrimp paste.
Place chicken on a cutting board and smash with a pestle.
Serve smashed chicken with sambal, lime, cucumber, and basil.

title: Es Teler 77
description: Jakarta's famous iced dessert with avocado, coconut, jackfruit, and condensed milk.
instructions: Scoop avocado into a glass.
Add jackfruit and coconut flesh.
Fill with crushed ice.
Drizzle with sweetened condensed milk and cocopandan syrup.
Stir and enjoy.

title: Devil's Rawon
description: Extremely spicy black beef soup — so hot it's called devil's soup.
ingredients: Salted eggs, bean sprouts for serving
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Reserve broth.
Extract kluwek flesh and grind to a paste.
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, and ginger.
Sauté spice paste with kluwek and lemongrass.
Add to broth and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season and serve with salted eggs and bean sprouts.

title: Balinese Mixed Rice
description: Balinese rice plate with various dishes — lawar, satay, sambal, crispy skin.
instructions: Prepare steamed rice.
Make lawar by mixing blanched vegetables with spiced grated coconut.
Grill sate lilit on lemongrass stalks.
Prepare sambal matah with raw shallots, chilies, and lime.
Arrange all components on a banana leaf plate.
Serve with rice in the center surrounded by all the dishes.

title: Indonesian Fruit Ice
description: Colorful medley of tropical fruits in sweet coconut milk and syrup.
instructions: Arrange all fruits in a tall glass.
Add nata de coco.
Fill with crushed ice.
Drizzle with rose syrup and sweetened condensed milk.
Stir gently and serve with a long spoon.

title: Beef Trotter Soup
description: Rich, collagen-packed soup from slow-cooked beef trotters.
ingredients: 1 kg beef trotters, cleaned and cut
Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 1 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper
instructions: Boil trotters for 3-4 hours until very tender and gelatinous.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and lime leaves.
Add to broth and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt.
Serve with spring onions, fried shallots, and lime wedges.

title: Jakarta Gado-Gado
description: Classic Jakarta gado-gado with smooth, sweet peanut sauce.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: 250 g roasted peanuts, 5 red chilies, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp sweet soy sauce, 1 tbsp tamarind water, salt, sugar, water
instructions: Blanch vegetables until just tender.
Grind peanut sauce ingredients until smooth and creamy.
Arrange vegetables, tofu, tempeh, rice cake, and egg on a plate.
Pour peanut sauce generously over everything.
Garnish with fried shallots and serve with crackers.

title: Noodle Soup
description: Yellow noodles in clear, savory broth with beef and fried wontons.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp coriander
instructions: Cook noodles until al dente. Drain.
Sauté spice paste until fragrant. Add to broth.
Add beef slices and cook briefly.
Add vegetables and simmer until just tender.
Place noodles in bowls, ladle broth and beef over top.
Serve with fried wontons, condiments on the side.

title: Makassar Pressed Banana
description: Makassar's signature flattened, grilled bananas with palm sugar syrup and ice cream.
ingredients: Palm sugar syrup: 200 g palm sugar, 100 ml water, pandan leaf
instructions: Grill plantains until softened and slightly charred.
Press each banana flat using a press or the back of a knife.
Make palm sugar syrup by boiling palm sugar, water, and pandan until dissolved.
Place pressed bananas on a plate.
Drizzle with palm sugar syrup.
Top with a scoop of ice cream and grated cheese if desired.

title: Scrambled Fried Rice
description: Messy, delicious fried rice where eggs are scrambled throughout.
instructions: Heat oil in a wok over very high heat.
Add garlic and stir-fry briefly.
Add rice and sweet soy sauce. Toss well.
Make a well in the center, crack in all 4 eggs.
Scramble the eggs vigorously, mixing with the rice.
Continue cooking until eggs are set and coat every grain.
Garnish with spring onions and fried shallots.

title: Martabak Ice Cream
description: Warm martabak manis served with ice cream, chocolate, and cheese.
ingredients: Toppings: chocolate sprinkles, crushed peanuts, grated cheese, sweetened condensed milk
instructions: Cook martabak until golden and fluffy with holes on top.
Spread generously with butter while hot.
Add chocolate, peanuts, cheese, and condensed milk.
Fold in half and cut into pieces.
Serve warm with a scoop of ice cream on top.

title: Grilled Oxtail Soup
description: Oxtail first grilled for smoky flavor, then simmered into rich soup.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 1 tbsp coriander
instructions: Marinate oxtail in sweet soy sauce for 30 minutes.
Grill oxtail until charred on all sides.
Boil grilled oxtail in water for 2 hours until tender.
Sauté spice paste and add to broth.
Add carrots and potatoes, simmer until tender.
Season and serve with fried shallots.

title: Round Fried Tofu
description: Jakarta's famous deep-fried round tofu balls — crispy outside, hollow inside.
instructions: Mash tofu until smooth.
Mix with tapioca, garlic powder, salt, and baking powder.
Shape into small balls.
Deep fry in medium-hot oil until golden and puffed.
Drain and serve with chili sauce.

title: Cendol Jelly Drink
description: Modern version of cendol using agar-agar jelly cubes.
ingredients: Green agar-agar jelly (pre-made or from packet)
instructions: Cut agar-agar jelly into small cubes.
Fill glasses with crushed ice.
Add jelly cubes.
Pour coconut milk over the ice.
Drizzle with palm sugar syrup.
Add durian paste for extra flavor if desired.

title: Padang Satay with Thick Sauce
description: Beef satay served with thick, spicy rice flour sauce instead of peanut sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp rice flour, beef broth, 8 red chilies, 4 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 2 cm ginger, 1 tbsp coriander, turmeric, salt
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Skewer the pieces.
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, coriander, and turmeric.
Cook spice paste with beef broth.
Add rice flour dissolved in water, stirring until thick.
Season with salt.
Grill beef skewers until charred.
Serve with thick sauce and crackers.

title: Sweet Potato Mochi
description: Soft, chewy mochi cakes filled with sweet potato paste.
ingredients: 150 g sweet potato, steamed and mashed
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with water and sweet potato.
Steam the dough for 20 minutes.
Knead until smooth and elastic.
Dust with cornstarch and shape into small balls.
Let cool and serve.

title: Stink Bean Fried Rice
description: Bold fried rice with stink beans (petai) — for adventurous eaters.
instructions: Fry stink beans briefly and set aside.
Stir-fry garlic and belacan until fragrant.
Add shrimp and cook until pink.
Scramble eggs to the side.
Add rice and sweet soy sauce.
Toss in stink beans and chilies.
Serve immediately.

title: Fruit Soup Ice
description: Refreshing mixed fruit dessert in sweet coconut milk soup.
instructions: Cut all fruits into bite-sized pieces.
Arrange fruits in glasses.
Fill with crushed ice.
Pour sweetened condensed milk and sugar syrup over the top.
Stir gently and serve with a spoon.

title: Padang Grilled Chicken
description: West Sumatra's turmeric-marinated grilled chicken over charcoal.
ingredients: Marinade: 5 cm turmeric, 3 cm ginger, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp coriander, 2 lemongrass stalks, salt
instructions: Grind marinade ingredients into a paste.
Coat chicken pieces with the paste and coconut milk.
Marinate for at least 2 hours.
Grill over charcoal, basting with sweet soy sauce.
Cook for 20-25 minutes until charred and cooked through.
Serve with steamed rice and chili sauce.

title: Clear Chicken Soto
description: Light, clear chicken soup with glass noodles and lime.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 6 shallots, 4 garlic cloves, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander
instructions: Boil chicken until tender. Remove and shred.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and lime leaves.
Add to broth and bring to a boil.
Strain broth for clarity.
Serve with shredded chicken, glass noodles, cabbage, bean sprouts, egg, and lime.

title: Noodle Martabak
description: Crispy savory pancake stuffed with noodles and eggs.
ingredients: Filling: 200 g yellow noodles, 4 eggs, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 5 green chilies, salt, pepper, sweet soy sauce
instructions: Cook noodles until done. Season with sweet soy sauce.
Mix noodles with beaten eggs, chopped shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Stretch dough paper-thin.
Place noodle-egg filling in center, fold into square.
Fry until golden and crispy on both sides.
Cut and serve with pickles.

title: Sumedang Fried Tofu
description: Famous West Javanese tofu — golden with light, airy texture inside.
instructions: Cut tofu into large pieces.
Soak in salt water for 15 minutes.
Drain and pat dry.
Deep fry in very hot oil until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with chili sauce.

title: Fruit Rujak Ice
description: Tropical fruits with spicy-sweet palm sugar sauce and ice.
ingredients: Mixed fruits: mango, pineapple, jicama, cucumber, unripe papaya
Rujak sauce: 200 g palm sugar, 5 red chilies, 2 tbsp peanuts, 1 tbsp tamarind, 100 ml water, shrimp paste (optional)
instructions: Cut all fruits into bite-sized pieces.
Grind palm sugar, chilies, peanuts, tamarind, and shrimp paste into a thick sauce.
Arrange fruits on a plate.
Serve sauce on the side for dipping.

title: Rujak-Spiced Grilled Chicken
description: Grilled chicken in spicy rujak-style paste — sweet, sour, and fiery.

Serve warm with a drizzle of coconut milk and a pinch of salt.

title: Smashed Chicken Rice

Fresh vegetables: cucumber, basil, long beans

Coat with flour and deep fry until crispy.
Make sambal by grinding chilies, garlic, and shrimp paste.
Smash the fried chicken with a pestle.

title: Grilled Beef Rib Soup

Boil grilled ribs in water for 2 hours until tender.
Sauté spice paste and add to broth.
Add carrots and potatoes, simmer until tender.
Season with salt.
Serve with rice and fried shallots.

title: Dawet Ice

Press through a strainer into ice water to form small jelly noodles.
Make palm sugar syrup by boiling palm sugar, water, and pandan leaf.
Heat coconut milk with salt and pandan until warm.
To serve: fill glass with shaved ice, add green jelly, drizzle with coconut milk and palm sugar syrup.

title: Cucur Cake

Let batter rest for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a wok. Pour batter into the center.
Fry until edges are crispy and center is cooked.
Drain and serve.

title: Herb Rice

Finely chop all herbs.
Mix rice with coconut, herbs, fried shallots, dried shrimp, and peanuts.
Season with lime juice and salt.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Madura Goat Soup

Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 6 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper, 3 candlenuts
instructions: Boil goat meat until tender. Reserve broth.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and lime leaves.
Add to broth and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt.
Serve with spring onions, fried shallots, and lime wedges.

title: Serabi with Kinca Sauce
description: Small coconut pancakes served with warm palm sugar sauce.
ingredients: Kinca sauce: 200 g palm sugar, 200 ml coconut milk, pandan leaf, pinch of salt
instructions: Mix flours, coconut milk, sugar, and yeast. Let rest 1 hour.
Heat a clay or non-stick pan.
Pour small rounds of batter and cover.
Cook until bottom is golden and top is set.
Make kinca sauce by boiling palm sugar, coconut milk, and pandan.
Serve serabi warm with kinca sauce.

title: Smashed Chicken with Raw Sambal

title: Mini Tumpeng

instructions: Cook rice with coconut milk and turmeric.

title: Passion Fruit Syrup Ice

title: Karo Roast Pork

title: Creamy Milk Soto

instructions: Boil beef until tender. Cut into cubes.

title: Extra Spicy Fried Rice

title: Makassar Rib Soup

description: Fried rice with goat meat in gulai-style curry paste.

instructions: Coat chicken with flour and deep fry until crispy.

title: Grilled Rib Soup Special
description: Rich Makassar soup with grilled ribs and keluak nuts.

title: Bebek Betutu Recipe: Authentic Balinese Slow-Cooked Duck
description: A legendary Balinese dish of whole duck stuffed with a rich spice paste, wrapped in banana leaves, and slow-cooked for hours until the meat falls off the bone.
instructions: Grind all spices (chilies, shallots, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, galangal, turmeric, kencur, shrimp paste) into a smooth paste.
Rub the spice paste all over the duck, inside and out. Let it marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Stuff the cavity with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaves.
Wrap the duck tightly in banana leaves, then in aluminum foil.
Bake in a preheated oven at 150°C for 5-6 hours, or until the meat is extremely tender.
Alternatively, cook in a traditional pit with hot coals for an authentic smoky flavor.
Unwrap carefully and serve with steamed rice, lawar, and sambal matah.

title: Soto Padang Recipe: Authentic Minangkabau Beef Soup
description: A comforting Minangkabau beef soup with rich, aromatic broth, crispy emping crackers, and tender beef slices — the iconic comfort food of West Sumatra.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 candlenuts, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper
instructions: Boil beef brisket and tendon in water until tender, about 2 hours. Reserve the broth.
Grind all spice paste ingredients until smooth.
Sauté the spice paste in oil until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and bay leaves. Stir until wilted.
Pour in the reserved beef broth. Add turmeric powder. Bring to a boil.
Add the cooked beef and tendon. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and sugar to taste.
Serve hot in bowls with rice vermicelli, fried potatoes, emping crackers, celery, spring onions, lime wedges, and sambal lado.

title: Rujak Cingur Recipe: Surabaya's Iconic Mixed Fruit Salad
description: Surabaya's famous fruit salad featuring a bold peanut-shrimp paste dressing, crunchy vegetables, and the signature cow snout (cingur) that gives the dish its name.
ingredients: 200 g cow snout (cingur), boiled until tender and sliced
100 g water spinach (kangkung), blanched and cut
Rujak dressing: 200 g roasted peanuts, 3 tbsp shrimp paste (petis), 2 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tsp tamarind, 100 ml warm water, 5 red chilies
instructions: Prepare the rujak dressing: grind peanuts until coarse. Mix with shrimp paste, palm sugar, tamarind dissolved in warm water, and ground chilies. Stir until smooth.
Boil cow snout until very tender, about 1.5 hours. Slice into thin strips.
Prepare all vegetables and fruits: slice cucumber, mango, pineapple. Blanch bean sprouts and water spinach. Cube potatoes and sweet potatoes.
Arrange all ingredients on a large plate or bowl.
Pour the rujak dressing generously over everything.
Toss gently to coat all ingredients with the dressing.
Garnish with fried shallots and serve with lontong.

title: Tekwan Recipe: Palembang Fish Soup Dumplings
description: Delicate fish dumplings in a light, aromatic shrimp broth — a beloved Palembang breakfast dish that showcases the city's mastery of fish-based cuisine.
ingredients: 500 g white fish fillets (mackerel or tenggiri), ground
Broth: 1.5 liters water, 200 g dried shrimp, 3 lemongrass stalks, 5 kaffir lime leaves, salt
Serving: rice vermicelli, sliced celery, fried shallots, sweet soy sauce, chili sauce
instructions: Grind fish fillets until smooth. Mix with tapioca flour, garlic, salt, and pepper. Add ice water gradually until dough is pliable but not sticky.
Bring water to a boil. Shape dough into small balls (about 2 cm) and drop into boiling water.
Cook until dumplings float to the surface, about 3-4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Prepare broth: boil dried shrimp with water, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves for 20 minutes. Strain and season.
Serve dumplings in bowls with rice vermicelli, hot broth, celery, fried shallots, sweet soy sauce, and chili sauce.

title: Nasi Liwet Recipe: Sundanese Coconut Rice Feast
description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk with aromatic spices — the centerpiece of Sundanese communal feasting that brings families together around a banana leaf-lined table.
ingredients: Side dishes: fried chicken, tofu, tempeh, hard-boiled eggs, sambal, lalapan (raw vegetables)
instructions: Heat oil in a rice cooker or heavy pot. Sauté lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, and galangal until fragrant.
Add washed rice and stir to coat with the aromatic oil.
Pour in coconut milk and water. Add salt. Stir well.
Cook as you would regular rice — either in a rice cooker or on the stovetop with lid on low heat.
Once cooked, fluff gently with a fork to distribute the aromatics.
Serve on a large banana leaf-lined table surrounded by side dishes for communal eating.

title: Babi Guling Recipe: Balinese Spit-Roasted Suckling Pig
description: Bali's most celebrated dish — whole suckling pig rubbed with a fiery spice paste and spit-roasted until the skin is crackling crisp and the meat impossibly tender.
ingredients: Spice paste: 20 red chilies, 15 shallots, 10 garlic cloves, 5 candlenuts, 5 cm galangal, 3 cm ginger, 3 cm turmeric, 2 cm kencur, 1 tbsp shrimp paste, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper
instructions: Grind all spice paste ingredients into a smooth paste.
Score the pig's skin in a crosshatch pattern. Rub the spice paste all over the inside of the cavity.
Stuff the cavity with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaves.
Sew or skewer the cavity closed. Rub the outside with salt.
Mount on a spit and roast over hot coals, turning continuously for 3-4 hours.
Baste occasionally with the rendered fat and spice juices.
The pig is done when the skin is golden-brown and crackling, and the meat pulls easily from the bone.
Carve and serve with steamed rice, lawar, sambal matah, and vegetables.

title: Tinutuan Recipe: Manado Mixed Porridge
description: A colorful Manado breakfast porridge combining rice, corn, pumpkin, sweet potato, and cassava — the 'bubur Manado' that represents North Sulawesi's diverse agricultural bounty.
ingredients: Accompaniments: fried salted fish, sautéed greens (kangkung), sambal roa, grated coconut
instructions: Bring water to a boil. Add rice and cook until it starts to break down, about 20 minutes.
Add corn kernels, pumpkin, sweet potato, and cassava.
Continue cooking until all ingredients are soft and the porridge is thick, about 20-30 minutes more.
Season with salt. The porridge should be thick but still have visible chunks of vegetables.
Serve hot with fried salted fish, sautéed greens, sambal roa, and grated coconut on the side.

title: Sate Klatak Recipe: Yogyakarta Iron Skewer Goat Satay
description: Yogyakarta's distinctive goat satay grilled on iron bicycle spokes — a uniquely Javanese street food that combines simple preparation with bold, smoky flavors.
ingredients: 500 g goat meat, cut into small cubes
Iron bicycle spokes or metal skewers
Bumbu: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander, salt
Gulai sauce: 400 ml coconut milk, 2 lemongrass stalks, 3 kaffir lime leaves, 2 cm galangal, ground spice paste (5 shallots, 3 garlic, 2 cm ginger, 1 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander)
instructions: Marinate goat meat cubes with ground bumbu for at least 1 hour.
Thread meat onto iron skewers (bicycle spokes).
Grill over hot charcoal, turning frequently, until cooked through and slightly charred, about 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare gulai sauce: sauté ground spice paste until fragrant. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. Pour in coconut milk and simmer until thickened.
Serve satay with gulai sauce poured over, sweet soy sauce, and steamed rice.

title: Soto Kudus Recipe: Central Java's Chicken Soup
description: A clear, aromatic chicken soup from Kudus — known for its distinctive sweetness and the unique addition of shredded chicken and fried potatoes.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm turmeric, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper
Sweet soy sauce (kecap manis) to taste
Serving: rice, fried potatoes, boiled eggs, spring onions, celery, fried shallots, lime
instructions: Boil whole chicken in water with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and bay leaves until tender, about 1 hour.
Remove chicken, shred the meat, and set aside. Reserve the broth.
Sauté ground spice paste until fragrant. Add to the broth.
Season broth with sweet soy sauce, salt, and sugar. The broth should be slightly sweet and golden.
Fry diced potatoes until crispy. Hard-boil eggs.
Serve bowls with rice, shredded chicken, fried potatoes, halved egg, spring onions, celery, and fried shallots.
Pour hot broth over and finish with lime juice.

title: Ayam Goreng Lengkuas Recipe: Galangal Fried Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken infused with galangal and turmeric — a Sundanese specialty where the aromatic spice coating creates an irresistible golden crust.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 100 g galangal, 5 cm turmeric, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 2 candlenuts, 1 tsp coriander, salt
instructions: Grind galangal, turmeric, shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and coriander into a smooth paste.
Boil chicken pieces with the spice paste, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves until almost cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Remove chicken and strain the remaining liquid. Reserve both.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Fry chicken pieces until golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry the strained spice paste in the same oil until crispy and golden.
Serve chicken topped with the crispy galangal flakes, accompanied by steamed rice and sambal.

title: Ikan Bakar Cobek Recipe: Stone Mortar Grilled Fish
description: Fresh fish grilled and served with a bold spice paste ground in a traditional stone mortar — a Javanese coastal specialty that showcases the art of sambal-making.
ingredients: 4 whole fish (snapper, mackerel, or tilapia), cleaned
Spice paste: 15 red chilies, 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm kencur, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tbsp shrimp paste, juice of 2 limes, salt
Steam rice and lalapan (raw vegetables) for serving
instructions: Score the fish and rub with salt and lime juice. Let marinate for 15 minutes.
Grind all spice paste ingredients in a stone mortar (cobek) until smooth but slightly coarse.
Grill fish over hot charcoal, basting with some of the spice paste, until cooked through and slightly charred.
Place grilled fish on a plate. Pour the remaining fresh spice paste over the top.
Serve immediately with steamed rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Sate Klatak Premium Recipe: Elevated Yogya Iron Skewer Satay
description: A premium version of Yogyakarta's iconic iron-skewer goat satay with wagyu beef option and artisanal gulai sauce.
ingredients: 500 g premium goat tenderloin or wagyu beef, cut into cubes
Marinade: 5 shallots, 3 garlic, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander, salt, 1 tbsp kecap manis
Artisanal gulai: 400 ml coconut cream, 2 lemongrass, 3 kaffir lime leaves, 2 cm galangal, ground paste (5 shallots, 3 garlic, 2 cm ginger, 1 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 candle nut)
Garnish: fried shallots, chopped celery, lime wedges
Side: nasi goreng kambing, es teh manis
instructions: Marinate meat cubes with ground marinade for 2 hours.
Thread onto iron skewers. Grill over premium charcoal until charred outside, pink inside for beef, fully cooked for goat.
Prepare artisanal gulai: toast spices, grind fine. Simmer coconut cream with lemongrass, kaffir lime, galangal, and spice paste until thick and fragrant.
Plate: drizzle gulai on plate, arrange skewers, garnish with fried shallots, celery, lime.
Serve with nasi goreng kambing and es teh manis.

title: Sayur Asem Recipe: Sundanese Tamarind Vegetable Soup
description: A refreshing Sundanese vegetable soup with a distinctive sweet-sour tamarind broth — the quintessential comfort food that showcases West Java's love for fresh vegetables.
ingredients: 200 g corn on the cob, cut into rounds
100 g long beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
2 tbsp tamarind paste dissolved in 200 ml water
Ground spice paste: 5 red chilies, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 2 cm galangal, 1 tsp shrimp paste, salt
instructions: Bring water to a boil. Add corn and peanuts. Cook for 10 minutes.
Add ground spice paste, bay leaves, and tamarind water. Stir well.
Add chayote and cook for 5 minutes.
Add long beans and cabbage. Cook until vegetables are tender but still have some crunch, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and sugar. The broth should be sweet, sour, and slightly spicy.
Serve hot with steamed rice and fried tempeh.

title: Opor Ayam Recipe: Javanese Coconut Chicken Curry
description: A mild, creamy coconut chicken curry that's the centerpiece of Lebaran (Eid) celebrations across Java — fragrant, comforting, and deeply traditional.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin, 4 candlenuts
Fried shallots and boiled eggs for serving
instructions: Grind all spice paste ingredients until smooth.
Heat oil in a pot. Sauté spice paste until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, and bay leaves. Stir until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces. Stir to coat with the spice paste.
Pour in coconut milk and water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook on low heat for 30-40 minutes until chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and sugar. Serve with steamed rice, ketupat, and fried shallots.

title: Kolak Pisang Recipe: Banana in Palm Sugar Coconut Soup
description: Sweet bananas and cassava in a warm palm sugar and coconut milk broth — the beloved Indonesian comfort dessert that's especially popular during Ramadan iftar.
instructions: Bring water to a boil. Add palm sugar and pandan leaves. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add cassava and sweet potato if using. Cook until almost tender, about 10 minutes.
Add banana slices. Cook for 3-5 minutes until just tender.
Pour in coconut milk. Add salt. Stir gently.
Heat through without boiling — the coconut milk should not separate.
Serve warm as a dessert or snack.

title: Bubur Sumsum Recipe: Javanese Rice Flour Porridge
description: A smooth, creamy rice flour porridge served with palm sugar syrup — a traditional Javanese dessert that's both humble and elegant in its simplicity.
ingredients: Palm sugar syrup: 200 g palm sugar, 100 ml water, 1 pandan leaf
Fried shallots or grated coconut for topping (optional)
instructions: Dissolve rice flour in coconut milk and water, stirring until smooth with no lumps.
Add salt and pandan leaf (if using in the porridge).
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens into a smooth porridge, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove pandan leaf. The porridge should be smooth, thick, and pourable.
Prepare palm sugar syrup: dissolve palm sugar in water with pandan leaf over low heat. Strain.
Serve porridge in bowls, drizzled with palm sugar syrup.

title: Es Campur Recipe: Indonesian Mixed Ice Dessert
description: A colorful medley of fruits, jellies, and sweet toppings drenched in coconut milk and condensed milk — Indonesia's most popular shaved ice dessert.
ingredients: Toppings: diced jackfruit, diced papaya, diced melon, grass jelly (cincau), nata de coco, attap chee (palm seeds), diced bread, red beans, syrup (cocopandan or rose)
instructions: Prepare all toppings: dice fruits, cut jelly into cubes, cook red beans until soft.
Fill a bowl or glass with shaved ice.
Arrange toppings over the ice in colorful layers.
Drizzle with coconut milk, condensed milk, and sugar syrup.
Finish with a splash of cocopandan or rose syrup for color.
Serve immediately with a long spoon and straw.

title: Bakso Urat Recipe: Indonesian Beef Tendon Meatball Soup
description: Giant meatballs filled with beef tendon in a rich, clear broth — the beloved Indonesian street food that combines bouncy meatballs with melting tendon filling.
ingredients: 200 g beef tendon, boiled until soft and diced
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp sugar
Broth: 2 liters beef broth, 2 lemongrass stalks, 3 kaffir lime leaves, salt
Serving: rice noodles, fried wontons, sliced celery, fried shallots, chili sauce, lime
instructions: Mix ground beef with tapioca flour, garlic, salt, pepper, and sugar. Add ice water gradually until mixture is smooth and bouncy.
Take a handful of meat mixture, flatten, place diced tendon in center, and seal into a large ball (about 8 cm diameter).
Bring water to a gentle simmer. Cook meatballs until they float, about 10 minutes.
Prepare broth: simmer beef broth with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves for 20 minutes.
Serve meatballs in bowls with rice noodles, hot broth, fried wontons, celery, fried shallots, chili sauce, and lime.

title: Nasi Rawon Recipe: East Java Black Nut Beef Rice
description: A rich, dark beef stew colored by the mysterious kluwek nut, served over rice — East Java's most distinctive and complex comfort food.
ingredients: 50 g kluwek nuts (keluak), shells removed, flesh soaked in warm water
Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin
Serving: steamed rice, bean sprouts, fried shallots, salted egg, sambal
instructions: Soak kluwek nuts in warm water for 30 minutes. Mash the flesh into a paste.
Grind all spice paste ingredients until smooth.
Heat oil in a pot. Sauté spice paste until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add kluwek paste. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes.
Add beef cubes. Stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in water. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 2-3 hours until beef is very tender.
Season with salt and sugar. The stew should be dark brown-black and rich.
Serve over steamed rice with bean sprouts, fried shallots, salted egg, and sambal.

title: Ayam Penyet Tempe Recipe: Smashed Chicken with Fermented Soybean
description: Crispy fried chicken and tempeh smashed with fiery sambal — the iconic East Javanese street food that combines protein powerhouse with bold chili paste.
ingredients: Ground spice paste for chicken: 5 shallots, 3 garlic, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander, turmeric, salt
Sambal: 15 red chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic, 1 tsp shrimp paste, salt, lime juice, sugar
Steamed rice, cucumber, cabbage for serving
instructions: Marinate chicken with ground spice paste for 1 hour.
Boil chicken until almost cooked. Remove and drain.
Fry tempeh until golden. Set aside.
Fry chicken until crispy and golden.
Grind sambal ingredients in a mortar until slightly coarse.
Place chicken and tempeh on a stone mortar. Smash with pestle to crack the surface.
Spoon sambal over the smashed chicken and tempeh.
Serve with steamed rice, cucumber, and cabbage.

title: Es Teler Avocado Recipe: Indonesian Avocado Ice Dessert
description: Creamy avocado blended with ice, coconut milk, and condensed milk — a uniquely Indonesian twist on avocado that transforms it into a refreshing dessert.
instructions: Scoop avocado flesh into a blender. Add a splash of coconut milk.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Fill a glass with shaved ice.
Pour the avocado mixture over the ice.
Drizzle with condensed milk, coconut milk, and sugar syrup.
Add chocolate syrup if desired for color contrast.
Serve immediately with a spoon and straw.

title: Sop Konro Bakar Recipe: Grilled Rib Beef Soup
description: A rich Makassar beef rib soup served with grilled ribs — the signature dish of South Sulawesi that combines smoky grilled meat with aromatic broth.
ingredients: 1 kg beef ribs, cut into sections
Spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp pepper, 5 red chilies
Serving: rice, emping crackers, lime, spring onions, celery
instructions: Boil beef ribs in water until tender, about 2 hours. Reserve the broth.
Grind spice paste ingredients until smooth.
Sauté spice paste until fragrant. Add to the broth with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer for 30 minutes. Season with sweet soy sauce and salt.
Meanwhile, grill the boiled ribs over charcoal until slightly charred and caramelized.
Serve broth in bowls with rice, topped with grilled ribs, emping crackers, lime, and herbs.

title: Pempek Palembang Recipe: Authentic Fish Cake with Vinegar Sauce
description: The original pempek from Palembang — fish cakes made with fresh mackerel and tapioca, served with the signature dark vinegar sauce (cuko) that defines this Sumatran delicacy.
ingredients: Cuko sauce: 200 ml water, 100 g palm sugar, 50 ml vinegar, 5 red chilies, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp shrimp paste, salt
Serving: rice noodles, cucumber, fried shallots
instructions: Grind mackerel until very smooth. Mix with tapioca flour, water, salt, and sugar until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Shape dough into various forms: long rolls (pempek lenjer), balls with egg filling (pempek telur), or flat rounds.
Boil in gently simmering water until they float and are cooked through, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove and let cool slightly. Can be served boiled or fried.
Prepare cuko: boil water with palm sugar, chilies, garlic, and shrimp paste. Add vinegar. Simmer until thick.
Serve pempek with cuko sauce, rice noodles, cucumber, and fried shallots.

title: Nasi Uduk Recipe: Betawi Coconut Rice
description: Fragrant Betawi steamed rice cooked in coconut milk with lemongrass and pandan leaves, served with fried chicken, tempeh, tofu, and spicy sambal.
ingredients: Fried chicken, fried tempeh, fried tofu, boiled eggs, sambal, emping crackers for serving
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Drain well.
Combine coconut milk, water, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, pandan, salt, galangal, and coriander in the rice cooker pot.
Add rice and stir to combine.
Cook in rice cooker until done. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork, removing the lemongrass and pandan leaves.
Serve with fried chicken, tempeh, tofu, boiled eggs, sambal, and emping crackers.

title: Nasi Padang Recipe: Minang Mixed Rice
description: A spread of steamed rice served with an array of Minangkabau dishes including rendang, gulai, sambal, and vegetables, representing the pinnacle of West Sumatran cuisine.
ingredients: Rendang: 500 g beef, coconut milk, spice paste
Gulai cubadak: young jackfruit in turmeric coconut sauce
Sambal lado merah: red chili paste
Kalio ayam: chicken in wet rendang sauce
instructions: Cook steamed rice until fluffy.
Prepare rendang: slow-cook beef in coconut milk and spice paste for 3-4 hours.
Cook gulai cubadak: simmer young jackfruit in turmeric coconut sauce.
Make sambal lado merah by grinding red chilies, shallots, and salt.
Boil cassava leaves until tender.
Form perkedel from mashed potato, shape into patties, and deep fry.
Make telur dadar: thin omelettes seasoned with turmeric.
Arrange all dishes around mounds of steamed rice on plates.
Serve family-style with all dishes visible.

title: Nasi Biryani Recipe: Indonesian Spiced Rice
description: A fragrant rice dish of Arab-Indonesian origin, featuring basmati rice cooked with aromatic spices, saffron, and tender meat, reflecting Aceh's rich trade history.
ingredients: 500 g chicken or lamb, cut into pieces
instructions: Marinate meat in yogurt, biryani spice, and salt for at least 1 hour.
Fry onions until golden and crispy. Set half aside for garnish.
In a heavy pot, heat oil and cook remaining onions until soft.
Add marinated meat and cook until sealed and lightly browned.
Add tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Parboil soaked rice in salted water for 5 minutes. Drain.
Layer rice over the meat mixture. Drizzle saffron milk over the top.
Sprinkle fried onions, mint, and coriander.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid. Cook on very low heat for 25-30 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then gently fold layers together when serving.

title: Nasi Kebuli Recipe: Arab-Indonesian Spiced Rice
description: A richly spiced rice dish from Aceh's Arab-Indonesian community, cooked with goat or lamb in a tomato-based sauce with Middle Eastern spices like cumin, cardamom, and cinnamon.
ingredients: Fried onions, raisins, and almonds for garnish
instructions: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry onions until golden.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add meat and brown on all sides.
Add pureed tomatoes, tomato paste, and all spices. Stir well.
Pour in meat broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer until meat is tender, about 1 hour.
Add drained rice to the pot. Stir to combine.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until rice is done.
Garnish with fried onions, raisins, and almonds before serving.

title: Nasi Ambeng Recipe: Javanese Ceremonial Rice
description: A Javanese ceremonial dish of steamed rice surrounded by an array of side dishes including shredded chicken, serundeng, shredded coconut, offal, and sambal, traditionally served during slametan communal feasts.
ingredients: 200 g ati ampela (liver and gizzard), diced and fried
instructions: Steam rice until fluffy.
Boil chicken with bay leaves and lemongrass. Shred when cool.
Make serundeng: toast grated coconut with ground spices until golden and dry.
Clean and dice liver and gizzard. Season and deep fry until crispy.
Toast shredded coconut with a pinch of salt until golden.
Hard-boil eggs, peel, and optionally fry until golden.
Make sambal goreng from diced potatoes, spices, and chili.
Arrange rice on a banana leaf-lined plate with all side dishes around it.
Serve communally, allowing guests to help themselves.

title: Nasi Bakar Recipe: Grilled Rice in Banana Leaf
description: Steamed rice mixed with spicy seasoning, wrapped in banana leaves, and grilled over charcoal until the leaves are charred and the rice is infused with smoky fragrance.
ingredients: Sambal and fried chicken for serving
instructions: Mix steamed rice with sliced chilies, shallots, kaffir lime leaves, salt, and sweet soy sauce.
Lay out banana leaf rectangles on a flat surface.
Place a portion of seasoned rice in the center of each leaf.
Top with shredded chicken or fish.
Fold the banana leaf tightly around the rice, securing with toothpicks.
Grill over medium charcoal heat for 5-7 minutes per side.
The banana leaves should be charred but not burnt.
Remove from grill, unwrap, and serve hot with sambal.

title: Nasi Lemak Recipe: Coconut Rice
description: Malaysia and Indonesia's beloved rice dish cooked in coconut milk with pandan leaves, served with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, egg, and cucumber. A breakfast staple across the Malay world.
ingredients: Sambal: 10 dried chilies, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp belacan, 1 tbsp sugar
instructions: Cook rice with coconut milk, water, pandan leaves, and salt in a rice cooker or pot.
Make sambal: soak dried chilies, blend with shallots, garlic, and belacan. Fry until oil separates.
Fry dried anchovies until crispy. Roast peanuts.
Boil eggs, peel, and halve.
Slice cucumber.
Mound rice on a plate, arrange sambal, anchovies, peanuts, egg, and cucumber around it.
Serve with fried chicken or rendang for a more substantial meal.

title: Nasi Dagang Recipe: Terengganu Rice
description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk with fenugreek seeds, served with fish curry and pickled vegetables. A beloved breakfast dish from the east coast of the Malay Peninsula.
ingredients: Fish curry: 500 g tuna or mackerel, 200 ml coconut milk, spice paste, turmeric, tamarind
Acar (pickled vegetables): cucumber, carrot, onion, chili in vinegar and sugar
instructions: Soak rice for 30 minutes. Drain.
Fry fenugreek seeds until fragrant. Add coconut milk, pandan, salt, and rice.
Cook rice until fluffy and all liquid is absorbed.
Prepare fish curry: cook fish in spiced coconut milk gravy with turmeric and tamarind.
Make acar: julienne vegetables and toss with vinegar, sugar, and salt.
Mound rice on plate, top with fish curry and acar.
Garnish with fried shallots and fresh herbs.

title: Nasi Tutug Oncom Recipe: Sundanese Oncom Rice
description: Steamed rice mixed with crushed fermented oncom (soybean cake), seasoned with shallots, garlic, chilies, and lime. A beloved Sundanese comfort food.
ingredients: Fried shallots, cucumber, and sambal for serving
instructions: Crumble oncom into small pieces.
Grind shallots, garlic, and chilies into a paste.
Sauté the spice paste in oil until fragrant.
Add crumbled oncom and cook until lightly toasted, about 5-7 minutes.
Mix the cooked oncom with steamed rice.
Season with salt and lime juice.
Serve with fried shallots, cucumber, and sambal.

title: Nasi Pecel Recipe: Peanut Sauce Rice
description: Steamed rice served with blanched vegetables and a rich peanut sauce dressing. A wholesome and nutritious dish popular across East Java.
ingredients: Pecel sauce: ground peanuts, palm sugar, tamarind, chili, salt
instructions: Roast peanuts until golden. Grind coarsely.
Cook pecel sauce: mix ground peanuts with palm sugar, tamarind, chili, and water.
Boil vegetables briefly until just tender. Drain well.
Arrange rice on a plate with vegetables around it.
Pour pecel sauce generously over the vegetables.
Add fried tempeh, tofu, and kerupuk.
Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.

title: Nasi Megono Recipe: Pekalongan Spiced Rice
description: A Central Javanese dish of rice mixed with finely chopped young jackfruit cooked in coconut milk and spices. A specialty of Pekalongan.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm turmeric
Fried chicken and sambal for serving
instructions: Boil young jackfruit until tender. Drain and chop finely.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and chopped jackfruit.
Cook until the liquid is absorbed and the mixture is dry.
Mix the megono with steamed rice.
Season with salt and serve with fried chicken and sambal.

title: Nasi Jamblang Recipe: Cirebon Teak Leaf Rice
description: Steamed rice wrapped in teak leaves and filled with various side dishes. A unique Cirebon specialty distinguished by the fragrant teak leaf wrapping.
ingredients: Side dishes: sambal goreng, fried chicken, tempeh, tofu, potato balado, semur eggs
instructions: Soak teak leaves in warm water until pliable.
Place steamed rice in the center of a teak leaf.
Add a selection of side dishes on top of the rice.
Wrap the teak leaf tightly around the rice and side dishes.
Secure with bamboo strips or toothpicks.
Steam briefly to meld the flavors.
Serve wrapped, allowing diners to unwrap at the table.

title: Nasi Jinggo Recipe: Small Bali Rice Pack
description: A small portion of rice with spicy chicken or pork, noodles, vegetables, and sambal, wrapped in banana leaf. Bali's iconic takeaway meal.
instructions: Cook chicken with Balinese spices — lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, and chili.
Shred the chicken when cool.
Boil yellow noodles and drain.
Blanch long beans briefly.
Place rice on banana leaf.
Top with shredded chicken, noodles, long beans, tempeh, and a generous spoonful of sambal.
Wrap tightly in banana leaf.

title: Nasi Kucing Recipe: Tiny Rice Portions
description: Miniature rice portions served on banana leaves with small amounts of various side dishes. Named for the tiny portions resembling a cat's meal.
ingredients: Small portions of: sambal goreng, orek tempe, shredded chicken, potato balado
instructions: Prepare all side dishes in small quantities.
Place a small mound of rice on a banana leaf.
Add tiny portions of each side dish.
Top with sambal.
Wrap in banana leaf.
Sell or serve individually.

title: Nasi Gandul Recipe: Pati Beef Soup Rice
description: A Central Javanese specialty of rice served with beef cooked in a sweet and savory coconut milk broth, a signature dish of Pati regency.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin
instructions: Blanch beef slices briefly. Drain.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal until fragrant.
Add beef and stir to coat.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Cook until beef is tender and the sauce thickens.
Season with sweet soy sauce and salt.
Serve the beef and sauce over steamed rice.
Garnish with fried shallots.

title: Nasi Bogana Recipe: Tegal Ceremonial Rice
description: A Tegalese ceremonial rice dish featuring rice wrapped in banana leaves with multiple side dishes including chicken curry, eggs, and vegetables.
ingredients: Chicken opor: 500 g chicken in coconut curry
instructions: Prepare chicken opor: simmer chicken in spiced coconut milk.
Make semur eggs: braise hard-boiled eggs in sweet soy sauce.
Cook sambal goreng: diced potatoes with chili paste.
Prepare orek tempe: sweet glazed tempeh strips.
Place rice on banana leaf with all side dishes.
Wrap tightly in banana leaf.
Steam briefly before serving.

title: Nasi Minyak Recipe: Oily Spiced Rice
description: A West Sumatran rice dish cooked in spiced oil and ghee, producing fragrant, golden grains. Often served at Minangkabau celebrations.
ingredients: Fried chicken or rendang for serving
instructions: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot.
Fry onions until golden. Add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, and cumin.
Add drained rice and stir to coat in the spiced oil.
Pour in warm water and salt.
Cover and cook on low heat until rice is done.
Rest for 10 minutes before fluffing.
Serve with fried chicken or rendang.

title: Gulai Ayam Recipe: Chicken Curry
description: Tender chicken pieces simmered in a rich, aromatic coconut milk curry with turmeric, galangal, and lemongrass. A Minangkabau classic.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 3 cm turmeric, 3 cm ginger, 2 candlenuts, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin
instructions: Sauté ground spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaves, and galangal until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and stir to coat with the spice paste.
Pour in coconut milk and water. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 30-40 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce thickens.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Gulai Kambing Recipe: Goat Curry
description: Tender goat meat slow-cooked in a rich, spiced coconut milk gravy. The Minangkabau version features a complex spice paste with turmeric and galangal.
ingredients: 1 kg goat meat, cut into pieces
Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 8 red chilies, 3 cm turmeric, 3 candlenuts, 1 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin
Salt and palm sugar to taste
instructions: Blanch goat meat to remove impurities. Drain.
Sauté spice paste with aromatics until fragrant and oil separates.
Add goat meat and stir to coat.
Pour in coconut milk and water.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5-2 hours until meat is very tender.
Season with salt and palm sugar.
Serve hot with steamed rice and vegetables.

title: Kalio Daging Recipe: Wet Rendang
description: The wet, saucy precursor to rendang — beef braised in spiced coconut milk that has not been reduced to dryness. Rich, creamy, and deeply flavored.
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut into chunks
Ground spice paste: 12 red chilies, 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 3 cm galangal, 3 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin, 4 candlenuts
Salt and palm sugar to taste
instructions: Toast ground spice paste without oil until fragrant.
Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaves, and galangal.
Pour in coconut milk and add beef.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Season when the sauce has reduced but is still wet and creamy.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Empal Gepuk Recipe: Smashed Beef
description: Thin beef slices that are boiled, smashed, marinated in sweet spices, and deep-fried until crispy. A Sundanese specialty with a distinctive sweet-spicy crust.
ingredients: 500 g beef shank, sliced 1 cm thick
Marinade: 8 shallots, 4 garlic cloves, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin, 2 tbsp palm sugar
instructions: Boil beef slices in water until tender, about 1 hour. Drain.
Arrange beef between cutting boards and pound gently with a mallet.
Grind marinade ingredients. Marinate beef for at least 2 hours.
Deep fry marinated beef until golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve with steamed rice, sambal, and fresh vegetables.

title: Empal Gentong Recipe: Cirebon Beef Soup
description: A Cirebon specialty of beef soup cooked in a clay pot (gentong) with a rich, aromatic broth. The slow clay pot cooking creates deep, complex flavors.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp pepper, 2 candlenuts
Fried shallots, spring onions, lime, sambal for serving
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Reserve the broth.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal.
Add beef broth and coconut milk.
Return beef to the pot and simmer for 30 minutes.
Adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with fried shallots, spring onions, lime, and sambal.
Traditionally cooked in a clay pot (gentong) over charcoal.

title: Bistik Jawa Recipe: Javanese Beefsteak
description: A Javanese interpretation of Western beefsteak, featuring tender beef in a sweet and savory brown gravy with potatoes and vegetables.
ingredients: 500 g beef sirloin, sliced 1 cm thick
instructions: Pound beef slices lightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Pan-fry beef until browned on both sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add beef broth, sweet soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce.
Add carrots and green beans. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry.
Return beef to the sauce.
Serve with fried potatoes, steamed rice, and vegetables.

title: Selat Solo Recipe: Solo Beef Steak
description: A Solo specialty of tender beef in a fragrant broth with vegetables and sweet soy sauce. The Solo version of bistik with a more refined, aromatic character.
instructions: Simmer beef in broth with spices until very tender.
Slice beef thinly when cool.
Strain broth and return to pan.
Add sweet soy sauce and vegetables to broth.
Cook until vegetables are tender.
Arrange sliced beef on plate.
Pour broth and vegetables over beef.
Serve with fried potatoes, hard-boiled egg, mustard, and pickles.

title: Bandeng Presto Recipe: Pressure-Cooked Milkfish
description: Milkfish (bandeng) cooked in a pressure cooker until the bones become soft and edible. A Semarang specialty that makes the notoriously bony milkfish completely digestible.
instructions: Clean and score the milkfish.
Season with salt, turmeric, ginger, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves.
Arrange in pressure cooker with water to cover.
Pressure cook for 30-40 minutes until bones are soft.
Remove carefully and let cool.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Serve with steamed rice and sambal.

title: Ayam Pop Recipe: Padang Pale Chicken
description: A Minangkabau chicken dish where the bird is poached in coconut water, resulting in pale, incredibly tender meat served with a fiery red sambal.
ingredients: Sambal: 10 red chilies, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp salt, juice of 1 lime, 2 tbsp coconut water
instructions: Poach chicken in coconut water with kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, and salt.
Simmer until chicken is cooked through but still juicy, about 20 minutes.
Remove chicken and let cool slightly.
Blend sambal ingredients until smooth.
Optionally, lightly grill the chicken for a smoky touch.
Serve chicken with sambal and steamed rice.

title: Ayam Percik Recipe: Malay Grilled Chicken
description: Chicken basted with a spiced coconut milk sauce while grilling, creating layers of flavor. A beloved Malay and Indonesian grilled chicken preparation.
instructions: Blend coconut milk with chili paste, coriander, cumin, turmeric, garlic, ginger, sugar, and salt.
Marinate chicken in half the sauce for at least 2 hours.
Grill chicken over medium heat.
Baste frequently with remaining sauce using a brush or banana leaf.
Grill for 30-40 minutes, turning and basting regularly.
The chicken should be charred in spots and coated with thick, caramelized sauce.
Serve with steamed rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Ayam Kecap Recipe: Sweet Soy Chicken
description: Chicken braised in sweet soy sauce (kecap manis) with shallots, garlic, ginger, and bay leaves. One of Indonesia's most popular home-cooked chicken dishes.
instructions: Heat oil in a wok. Fry shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and brown lightly.
Add ginger, bay leaves, and water.
Pour in sweet soy sauce. Stir well.
Simmer until chicken is cooked through and sauce thickens.
Season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fried shallots and serve with steamed rice.

title: Ayam Kodok Recipe: Stuffed Roasted Chicken
description: A whole chicken stuffed with a savory mixture of ground meat, vegetables, and spices, then roasted until golden. A festive dish for special occasions.
ingredients: Filling: 300 g ground chicken, 100 g shrimp, diced carrots, green beans, spring onions
instructions: Carefully debone the whole chicken, keeping the skin intact.
Prepare filling: mix ground chicken, shrimp, vegetables, garlic, egg, soy sauce, oyster sauce.
Stuff the filling into the chicken cavity.
Sew or tie the opening shut.
Brush chicken with oil and seasoning.
Roast at 180°C for 1-1.5 hours until golden and cooked through.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Serve with steamed rice and vegetables.

title: Bebek Goreng Recipe: Fried Duck
description: Duck marinated in a complex spice paste, then deep-fried until crispy. The signature of Madura and Javanese cooking, featuring intensely flavored, crispy-skinned duck.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 10 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 5 candlenuts, 3 cm turmeric, 3 cm galangal, 3 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin, 3 lemongrass stalks
Sambal and fresh vegetables for serving
instructions: Grind all spice paste ingredients.
Boil duck pieces with spice paste until tender, about 45 minutes.
Remove duck and drain well.
Deep fry duck in hot oil until golden and very crispy, about 10-15 minutes.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve with steamed rice, sambal, and fresh vegetables.

title: Babi Kecap Recipe: Braised Pork in Sweet Soy
description: Pork belly slow-braised in sweet soy sauce with garlic, ginger, and spices. A beloved dish in Bali's non-Muslim communities and North Sulawesi.
ingredients: 500 g pork belly, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat oil and fry shallots and garlic until golden.
Add ginger, galangal, bay leaves, and five-spice powder.
Add pork belly and brown on all sides.
Pour in sweet soy sauce and water.
Braise on low heat for 1-1.5 hours until pork is very tender.
The sauce should reduce to a thick, glossy coating.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Saksang Recipe: Batak Spicy Pork
description: A Batak specialty of pork cooked in a rich, spicy coconut milk sauce with andaliman pepper. The signature spice of Batak cuisine gives this dish its distinctive tingling sensation.
ingredients: 1 kg pork belly or shoulder, cut into chunks
1 tsp andaliman pepper (or Sichuan pepper as substitute)
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, chilies, ginger, galangal, and turmeric into a paste.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass until fragrant.
Add pork and cook until sealed.
Pour in coconut milk.
Simmer on low heat for 1.5-2 hours.
Add andaliman pepper in the last 15 minutes.
Season with salt.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Lawar Recipe: Balinese Mixed Vegetables
description: A Balinese dish of finely chopped vegetables mixed with grated coconut, spices, and sometimes minced meat. A colorful, aromatic salad-like preparation central to Balinese cuisine.
ingredients: 100 g young jackfruit, boiled and shredded
Spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 2 cm ginger, 1 cm turmeric
instructions: Prepare all vegetables: finely chop long beans, shred jackfruit and cabbage.
Cook minced pork with spices if using.
Grind spice paste ingredients.
Mix vegetables with spice paste and grated coconut.
Add cooked pork if using.
Season with salt and lime juice.
Top with fried shallots.
Serve at room temperature with rice.

title: Botok Recipe: Steamed Coconut Dish
description: A Javanese preparation of grated coconut mixed with spices and various fillings (tempeh, oncom, fish, or tofu), wrapped in banana leaves and steamed.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, chilies, and turmeric into a paste.
Mix grated coconut with the spice paste and crumbled tempeh or oncom.
Season with salt.
Place portions on banana leaves.
Wrap tightly.
Steam for 20-25 minutes.
Serve as a side dish with steamed rice.

title: Buntil Recipe: Leaf-Wrapped Roll
description: Cassava or taro leaves filled with spiced grated coconut and sometimes fish or shrimp, wrapped into parcels and simmered in coconut milk.
instructions: Blanch cassava leaves until pliable.
Grind shallots, garlic, chilies, and galangal.
Mix grated coconut with spice paste and dried shrimp.
Place filling on each leaf and fold into parcels.
Arrange parcels in a pan.
Pour coconut milk over the parcels.
Simmer for 20-30 minutes until coconut milk reduces.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Pepes Ikan Recipe: Steamed Fish in Banana Leaf
description: Fish fillets seasoned with a vibrant spice paste, wrapped in banana leaves, and steamed or grilled. A Sundanese method that keeps fish moist and fragrant.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, chilies, turmeric, and ginger into a paste.
Mix spice paste with sliced lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, salt, and lime juice.
Coat fish fillets thoroughly with the spice mixture.
Wrap each fillet in banana leaf.
Steam for 20-25 minutes or grill over charcoal.
Serve directly in the banana leaf wrapper.

title: Pepes Ayam Recipe: Steamed Chicken in Banana Leaf
description: Chicken pieces marinated in a turmeric-based spice paste, wrapped in banana leaves, and steamed or grilled until tender and fragrant.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, turmeric, ginger, galangal, and chilies into a paste.
Marinate chicken in spice paste, kaffir lime leaves, salt, and lime juice for 1 hour.
Wrap each piece in banana leaf.
Steam for 30-35 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Optionally, grill briefly for a smoky touch.
Serve in the banana leaf with steamed rice.

title: Arsik Recipe: Batak Spiced Carp
description: A Batak specialty of carp or goldfish cooked in a rich, yellow-orange spice sauce with andaliman pepper and torch ginger flower (bunga kantan).
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, turmeric, ginger, and galangal.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and sliced torch ginger flower.
Place scored fish in the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes.
Add andaliman pepper.
Serve with steamed rice and vegetables.

title: Cakalang Fufu Recipe: Smoked Skipjack Tuna
description: Skipjack tuna traditionally smoked over coconut husk fire, producing intensely flavored, dark, firm fish. A Manado preservation tradition and culinary staple.
ingredients: Sauce: 10 red chilies, 5 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp lime juice, salt
instructions: If smoking from fresh: clean skipjack, salt, and smoke over coconut husk for 2-3 hours.
If using pre-smoked: shred the fish and remove bones.
Grind chilies, shallots, and garlic for the sambal.
Mix sambal with lime juice.
Serve shredded smoked fish with sambal and steamed rice.
Also delicious mixed into dabu-dabu (Manado salsa).

title: Ayam Tangkap Recipe: Aceh Fried Chicken
description: Acehnese fried chicken seasoned with a complex spice paste featuring curry leaves, galangal, and turmeric, then deep-fried with crispy herb leaves.
instructions: Grind turmeric, galangal, shallots, garlic, cumin, and coriander into a paste.
Marinate chicken with spice paste and salt for at least 2 hours.
Deep fry chicken until golden and crispy.
In the last minutes of frying, add curry leaves to the oil.
The curry leaves will become crispy and fragrant.
Drain chicken with curry leaves.
Serve with steamed rice and sambal.

title: Tongseng Recipe: Solo Goat Soup
description: A Solo specialty of goat meat in a sweet, spicy, coconut milk-based broth with vegetables. Distinguished from sate by its soupy presentation and sweeter flavor profile.
