instructions: Boil goat meat until tender. Reserve broth.
Sauté shallots, garlic, chilies, turmeric, and ginger.
Add goat meat and stir.
Pour in coconut milk and some broth.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Add tomatoes and cabbage.
Season with sweet soy sauce, salt, and sugar.
Serve hot with fried shallots and steamed rice.

title: Tengkleng Recipe: Solo Goat Bone Soup
description: A frugal Solo dish made from goat bones, offal, and remaining meat, simmered in a fragrant coconut milk broth. Proof that the best flavors come from humble ingredients.
ingredients: 1 kg goat bones with some meat attached
Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 3 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander
instructions: Clean and blanch goat bones and offal.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal.
Add bones and offal. Stir to coat.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 1-1.5 hours until flavors meld.
Add coconut milk. Cook for another 15 minutes.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve with fried shallots, spring onions, and steamed rice.

title: Soto Madura Recipe: Madura Chicken Soup
description: A Madurese chicken soup distinguished by its dark, kluwek-based broth. The black nut (kluwek) gives this soto its signature color and earthy, complex flavor.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 candlenuts, 1 tsp coriander
Fried potatoes, hard-boiled egg, rice noodles, spring onions, lime, sambal
instructions: Boil chicken until tender. Shred meat. Reserve broth.
Soak kluwek meat in warm water. Mash into a paste.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Add kluwek paste and stir well.
Pour in chicken broth and coconut milk.
Add shredded chicken.
Cook until heated through and broth darkens.
Serve with fried potatoes, egg, rice noodles, spring onions, lime, and sambal.

title: Soto Medan Recipe: Medan Chicken Soup
description: A Medan specialty of chicken soup with a rich, yellow coconut milk broth, featuring shredded chicken, vermicelli, and hard-boiled egg.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander
Spring onions, fried shallots, lime, emping crackers
instructions: Boil chicken until tender. Shred meat. Reserve broth.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Add broth and coconut milk.
Return shredded chicken.
Cook until heated through.
Season with salt.
Serve over rice vermicelli with egg, potatoes, spring onions, fried shallots, lime, and emping.

title: Soto Solo Recipe: Solo Chicken Soup
description: A refined Solo chicken soup with a clear, aromatic broth. Known for its delicate flavor and elegant presentation, reflecting Solo's royal court culinary traditions.
instructions: Boil chicken in water with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, ginger, and galangal.
Skim foam regularly for a clear broth.
Remove chicken when cooked. Shred meat.
Strain broth.
Return shredded chicken to clear broth.
Season with salt.
Serve in individual bowls with perkedel, egg, spring onions, fried shallots, and lime.

title: Sop Saudara Recipe: Makassar Beef Soup
description: A Makassar specialty of beef soup with a rich, spiced broth, served with ketupat (rice cake), crispy shallots, and a fiery sambal.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp pepper, 2 candlenuts
Fried shallots, spring onions, lime, sambal
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Reserve broth.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal.
Add beef broth and coconut milk.
Return beef and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt.
Serve over ketupat with fried shallots, spring onions, lime, and sambal.

title: Sop Kambing Recipe: Goat Soup
description: A hearty goat soup with a clear, aromatic broth seasoned with nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon. A warming comfort food popular across Indonesia.
ingredients: Spring onions, fried shallots, lime, sambal
instructions: Boil goat meat until tender. Reserve broth.
In the broth, add shallots, garlic, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Cook until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with fried shallots, spring onions, lime, and sambal.
Enjoy with steamed rice or bread.

title: Brongkos Recipe: Java Beef Tofu Soup
description: An East Javanese specialty of beef and tofu in a dark, spiced coconut milk broth. The distinctive dark color comes from kluwek (black nut).
ingredients: 200 g firm tofu, cubed and fried
Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 2 cm ginger, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp coriander
instructions: Soak kluwek in warm water and mash.
Boil beef until tender.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal.
Add kluwek paste and stir.
Add beef and coconut milk.
Simmer until flavors meld.
Add fried tofu.
Serve with steamed rice and sambal.

title: Brenebon Recipe: Manado Bean Soup
description: A Manado specialty of red kidney beans in a clear, spiced broth with vegetables. A hearty, nutritious soup reflecting Manado's love of simple, bold flavors.
ingredients: 300 g red kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Cook soaked beans until tender, about 45 minutes.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and ginger.
Add vegetables and water.
Simmer until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with fried shallots, spring onions, lime, and steamed rice.

title: Sayur Lodeh Recipe: Vegetable Coconut Soup
description: An assortment of vegetables simmered in a mild, coconut milk-based broth with turmeric and aromatic spices. A comforting Javanese everyday dish.
instructions: Parboil harder vegetables (jackfruit, chayote) until partially tender.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and turmeric.
Add lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Pour in coconut milk.
Add all vegetables.
Simmer until vegetables are tender and flavors meld.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve with steamed rice and sambal.

title: Pallubasa Recipe: Makassar Beef Soup
description: A rich Makassar beef soup with coconut milk, toasted coconut, and a blend of spices. The toasted coconut gives pallubasa its distinctive nutty depth.
ingredients: 100 g grated coconut, toasted until golden
Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm turmeric, 1 tsp pepper
instructions: Boil beef until tender. Reserve broth.
Toast grated coconut in a dry pan until golden brown.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Add beef broth, coconut milk, and toasted coconut.
Return beef and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt.
Serve with fried potatoes, spring onions, and lime.

title: Pindang Recipe: Palembang Fish Soup
description: A Palembang specialty of fish cooked in a clear, sour-spicy broth with tamarind, turmeric, and tomatoes. The sourness preserves the fish and creates a refreshing soup.
ingredients: 500 g fish (mackerel or tilapia), cut into pieces
instructions: Boil water with turmeric, galangal, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Add fish pieces.
Add tomatoes and tamarind juice.
Simmer until fish is cooked through.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Asam Pedas Recipe: Sour Spicy Fish
description: Fish simmered in a fiery, sour tomato-based broth with tamarind, torch ginger, and a generous amount of chili. A bold, assertive dish from Palembang.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, chilies, and turmeric.
Sauté spice paste until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook until they break down.
Pour in water and tamarind paste.
Add vegetables and cook until tender.
Add fish fillets.
Simmer until fish is cooked.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Semur Jengkol Recipe: Jengkol Stew
description: Jengkol (dogfruit) slow-braised in a sweet, dark soy sauce-based gravy with warm spices. A polarizing dish — beloved by fans for its unique, pungent flavor.
instructions: Boil jengkol until tender. Pound lightly to flatten.
Heat oil and sauté shallots and garlic.
Add jengkol and stir.
Pour in sweet soy sauce and water.
Add nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon.
Braise on low heat until sauce thickens.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Krengsengan Recipe: Mutton Stew
description: An East Javanese specialty of mutton or lamb in a thick, dark sauce made from chili, tomato, and sweet soy sauce. Bold, sweet, and spicy.
instructions: Boil mutton until tender. Reserve broth.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add mutton and sweet soy sauce.
Pour in some broth.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve with fried shallots and steamed rice.

title: Kaledo Recipe: Donggala Beef Soup
description: A Donggala specialty of beef soup with a clear broth, typically served with cassava and chili sambal. Simple yet deeply satisfying.
ingredients: Sambal, spring onions, lime for serving
instructions: Boil beef in water until tender, about 1 hour.
Add cassava and cook until soft.
Add shallots, garlic, and ginger.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with sambal, spring onions, and lime.
Enjoy with steamed rice.

title: Sup Sarang Burung Recipe: Bird Nest Soup
description: A luxurious soup made with edible bird's nests in a clear, savory chicken broth. Prized in Chinese-Indonesian cuisine for its texture and perceived health benefits.
instructions: Soak bird's nest in water for 4-6 hours until expanded.
Simmer in chicken broth for 15-20 minutes.
Add beaten egg whites, stirring gently to create wisps.
Season with sesame oil, white pepper, and salt.
Garnish with spring onions and chicken strips.
Serve hot in individual bowls.

title: Bak Kut Teh Recipe: Pork Rib Soup
description: A Chinese-Indonesian herbal pork rib soup simmered with star anise, cinnamon, and medicinal herbs. A warming, medicinal soup popular in Indonesian Chinese communities.
ingredients: 500 g pork ribs, cut into pieces
Chinese herbs: dang shen, yu zhu (optional)
Rice or you tiao (fried dough) for serving
instructions: Blanch pork ribs. Drain.
Combine all ingredients in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 1.5-2 hours until pork is very tender.
Season with salt and soy sauce.
Serve hot with rice or fried dough sticks.

title: Sop Tunjang Sapi Recipe: Beef Trotter Soup
description: Beef trotters pressure-cooked until the collagen dissolves into a rich, gelatinous broth. A nourishing soup prized for its collagen content and warming properties.
ingredients: Spring onions, fried shallots, lime, sambal
instructions: Clean and blanch beef trotters.
Pressure cook with water, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and lemongrass for 40 minutes.
Release pressure and check tenderness.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with spring onions, fried shallots, lime, and sambal.
Enjoy with steamed rice.

title: Soto Babat Recipe: Tripe Soup
description: A soto variant featuring beef tripe (babat) in a yellow, turmeric-based broth. The tripe is simmered until tender and served with traditional soto accompaniments.
ingredients: 500 g beef tripe, cleaned and diced
Ground spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 2 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander
Fried potatoes, hard-boiled egg, spring onions, lime, sambal
instructions: Clean tripe thoroughly. Boil until tender, about 1 hour.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Add water and turmeric.
Return tripe and simmer.
Season with salt.
Serve with fried potatoes, egg, spring onions, lime, and sambal.

title: Soto Ceker Recipe: Chicken Feet Soup
description: A Sunda specialty of chicken feet simmered in a spiced broth until collagen-rich and tender. A humble yet deeply satisfying comfort food.
ingredients: Fried potatoes, rice vermicelli, spring onions, lime, sambal
instructions: Clean chicken feet and blanch.
Simmer with water, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric, shallots, and garlic for 1-1.5 hours.
The feet should be very tender and the broth gelatinous.
Season with salt.
Serve with fried potatoes, rice vermicelli, spring onions, lime, and sambal.

title: Sayur Oyong Recipe: Luffa Soup
description: A simple, light Javanese soup of luffa gourd (oyong) in a clear, mild broth with garlic and shallots. Perfect for hot days and light meals.
instructions: Heat oil and sauté shallots and garlic.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Add luffa slices.
Cook until luffa is tender but still slightly firm.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with fried shallots and steamed rice.
Add shrimp or egg for extra protein.

title: Sayur Bayam Recipe: Spinach Soup
description: A light, clear Javanese spinach soup with corn, shallots, and garlic. One of the simplest and most nutritious Indonesian everyday dishes.
ingredients: 1 corn on the cob, cut into rounds
instructions: Heat oil and sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add water and corn rounds.
Bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes.
Add spinach and cook briefly until just wilted.
Season with salt and sugar.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

title: Sate Kambing Recipe: Goat Satay
description: Skewered goat meat grilled over charcoal and served with a sweet soy sauce-based dipping sauce. A beloved Indonesian street food, especially popular in Solo and Yogyakarta.
ingredients: 500 g goat meat, cut into cubes
Sweet soy sauce for basting and dipping
instructions: Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes.
Thread goat meat onto skewers.
Grill over hot charcoal, turning frequently.
Baste with sweet soy sauce while grilling.
Grill until charred but still juicy.
Serve with sweet soy sauce, sliced shallots, diced tomatoes, chilies, and lime juice.

title: Sate Taichan Recipe: Spicy Chicken Satay
description: A Sundanese-style chicken satay served without the traditional peanut sauce — instead paired with a fiery sambal of crushed chilies and lime. Pure, clean flavors.
ingredients: 500 g chicken breast, cut into cubes
Marinade: lime juice, salt, garlic powder
Sambal: 15 bird's eye chilies, 3 garlic cloves, salt, lime juice, a little water
instructions: Marinate chicken cubes in lime juice, salt, and garlic powder for 30 minutes.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning frequently.
Grill until cooked through with nice char marks.
Make sambal: crush chilies and garlic with salt.
Mix in lime juice and a little water.
Serve satay with sambal and lime wedges.

title: Sate Udang Recipe: Shrimp Satay
description: Large shrimp skewered and grilled over charcoal, basted with a sweet and spicy glaze. A seafood variation that showcases Indonesia's coastal culinary traditions.
ingredients: 500 g large shrimp, peeled and deveined
instructions: Thread shrimp onto skewers.
Mix sweet soy sauce, chili sauce, lime juice, and garlic for the glaze.
Brush shrimp with glaze.
Grill over medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes per side.
Brush with more glaze while grilling.
Serve with lime wedges and steamed rice.

title: Sate Babi Recipe: Pork Satay
description: Pork skewers marinated in a complex Balinese spice paste and grilled over charcoal. A specialty of Bali and North Sulawesi's non-Muslim communities.
ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder, cut into cubes
Marinade: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm turmeric, 2 cm ginger, 3 red chilies, 1 tsp coriander, salt
instructions: Grind marinade ingredients into a paste.
Marinate pork cubes in spice paste for at least 2 hours.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal, turning frequently.
Baste with sweet soy sauce while grilling.
Grill until caramelized and cooked through.
Serve with steamed rice and sambal.

title: Sate Maranggi Recipe: Sunda Beef Satay
description: A Sundanese beef satay marinated in a sweet soy and spice mixture, grilled until caramelized. Distinguished by its sweet, sticky glaze and tender beef.
ingredients: 500 g beef tenderloin, cut into cubes
Marinade: 4 tbsp sweet soy sauce, 2 shallots minced, 2 garlic cloves minced, 1 cm ginger grated, 1 tsp coriander, salt
Sliced tomatoes, shallots, chilies for serving
instructions: Marinate beef cubes in sweet soy sauce, shallots, garlic, ginger, coriander, and salt for at least 2 hours.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over hot charcoal.
Baste with remaining marinade while grilling.
Grill until caramelized on the outside.
Serve with sliced tomatoes, shallots, and chilies.

title: Sate Ponorogo Recipe: Ponorogo Satay
description: A Ponorogo specialty of chicken satay served with a thick, savory peanut sauce and rice cake (lontong). The peanut sauce is the star — rich, thick, and deeply flavored.
ingredients: 500 g chicken thigh, cut into cubes
Peanut sauce: 200 g roasted peanuts ground, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 2 tbsp sweet soy sauce, water
instructions: Thread chicken onto skewers.
Grill until cooked through with nice char.
Make peanut sauce: sauté shallots, garlic, and chilies. Add ground peanuts and sweet soy sauce.
Add water and cook until thick.
Serve satay with peanut sauce over sliced lontong.
Garnish with fried shallots.

title: Sate Blora Recipe: Blora Chicken Satay
description: A Blora specialty where chicken satay is served with a distinctive peanut sauce containing petis (black shrimp paste), giving it a deeper, more complex flavor.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: 200 g roasted peanuts, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, 2 tbsp petis (black shrimp paste), sweet soy sauce
instructions: Thread chicken onto skewers and grill until cooked.
Make peanut sauce with petis as the distinguishing ingredient.
The petis gives the sauce a darker color and more complex, slightly funky flavor.
Serve over sliced lontong with the distinctive peanut sauce.

title: Sate Ambal Recipe: Klaten Chicken Satay
description: A Klaten specialty where chicken satay is served with a unique peanut sauce made from tempeh and ground peanuts. The tempeh gives the sauce a distinctive earthy depth.
ingredients: Sauce: 100 g tempeh, 100 g roasted peanuts, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, sweet soy sauce, water
instructions: Grill chicken satay until cooked.
Make sauce: fry tempeh until golden, then grind with peanuts, shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Add sweet soy sauce and water.
Cook until thick.
Serve satay with the unique tempeh-peanut sauce over sliced lontong.

title: Sate Matang Recipe: Aceh Beef Satay
description: An Acehnese beef satay served with a rich, spicy peanut sauce and a clear beef broth on the side. The accompanying broth sets it apart from other satay varieties.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: 200 g roasted peanuts, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 8 red chilies, sweet soy sauce
instructions: Thread beef onto skewers and grill until charred.
Make peanut sauce with a spicy kick.
Prepare a small bowl of clear beef broth.
Serve satay with peanut sauce, lontong, and the broth on the side.
Dip or sip the broth between bites.

title: Otak Otak Recipe: Grilled Fish Cake
description: Fish paste mixed with tapioca starch and spices, wrapped in banana leaves, and grilled over charcoal. A beloved Indonesian snack with a bouncy, savory character.
instructions: Blend fish into a smooth paste.
Mix with tapioca starch, shallots, garlic, egg whites, salt, and sugar.
Beat the mixture until sticky and bouncy.
Spread a thin layer of fish paste on banana leaf.
Roll into a thin cylinder and secure the ends.
Grill over charcoal for 5-7 minutes, turning frequently.
Serve hot with peanut sauce.

title: Ikan Bakar Bumbu Rujak Recipe: Grilled Fish with Rujak Spice
description: Fish marinated in a spicy, sweet rujak-style spice paste and grilled over charcoal. The rujak bumbu creates a fiery, tangy, and sweet coating.
ingredients: Spice paste: 8 red chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm galangal, 2 cm turmeric, 2 cm ginger
instructions: Score the fish deeply on both sides.
Grind spice paste ingredients.
Mix with palm sugar, tamarind juice, and sweet soy sauce.
Coat the fish thoroughly with the spice mixture.
Wrap in banana leaf.
Grill over charcoal for 8-10 minutes per side.
Baste with remaining spice paste.
Serve with lime wedges and steamed rice.

title: Ayam Cincane Recipe: Kalimantan Grilled Chicken
description: A Dayak specialty of chicken grilled in a rich, spicy sauce made from chili, ginger, and lemongrass. The sauce is applied repeatedly during grilling for intense flavor.
ingredients: Spice paste: 10 red chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 3 lemongrass stalks
instructions: Grind spice paste ingredients.
Marinate chicken in spice paste, sweet soy sauce, oil, and salt for at least 2 hours.
Grill over charcoal.
Baste repeatedly with remaining spice paste.
Grill until deeply charred and cooked through.
Serve with steamed rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Babi Panggang Karo Recipe: Karo Roasted Pork
description: A Batak Karo specialty of pork roasted with andaliman pepper and spices, served with a rich blood sauce (marsik). One of Indonesia's most distinctive pork dishes.
ingredients: Marsik (blood sauce): pig's blood, vinegar, salt, spices
instructions: Marinate pork with ground shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, andaliman pepper, and salt.
Let marinate overnight.
Roast in oven at 180°C for 1.5-2 hours until crispy outside.
Prepare marsik: mix fresh pig's blood with vinegar, salt, and ground spices.
Slice roasted pork.
Serve with marsik sauce and steamed rice.

title: Se'i Recipe: Timor Smoked Meat
description: A Timorese specialty of pork or beef smoked over a traditional wood fire pit. The slow smoking process creates intensely flavored, tender meat with a distinctive smoky character.
ingredients: 1 kg pork or beef, cut into long strips
Traditional smoking wood (kayu jati or coconut husk)
instructions: Salt meat strips generously.
Hang strips over a smoking pit.
Smoke for 4-6 hours over low, smoldering wood.
The meat should be dark, firm, and intensely smoky.
Slice thinly and serve with steamed rice.
Also served with fresh sambal.

title: Cakalang Woku Recipe: Manado Spiced Tuna
description: Skipjack tuna cooked in a vibrant, aromatic woku spice paste featuring lemongrass, ginger, and lime leaves. A signature Manado preparation.
ingredients: 500 g skipjack tuna, cut into chunks
Ground spice paste: 10 red chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm turmeric, 3 cm ginger, 5 candlenuts
instructions: Sauté spice paste with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, ginger, and galangal until fragrant.
Add tuna chunks.
Stir to coat fish with spices.
Cook on medium heat until fish is done.
Season with salt and lime juice.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Holat Recipe: Mandailing Grilled Fish
description: A Mandailing Batak specialty of fish marinated in andaliman pepper and spices, then grilled over charcoal. The andaliman gives it a distinctive numbing, citrusy flavor.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, and andaliman pepper into a paste.
Score the fish and rub with spice paste.
Let marinate for 30 minutes.
Grill over charcoal until cooked through.
Baste with lime juice while grilling.
Serve with steamed rice and fresh vegetables.

title: Na Tinombur Recipe: Batak Grilled Catfish
description: A Batak specialty of catfish (lele) marinated in a spicy andaliman and tomato-based sauce, then grilled. The marinade doubles as a dipping sauce.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, chilies, and andaliman pepper.
Mix with chopped tomatoes, salt, and lime juice.
Score catfish and coat with the mixture.
Grill over charcoal.
Baste with remaining sauce while grilling.
Serve with steamed rice and the grilled sauce.

title: Cilok Recipe: Tapioca Ball Snack
description: Chewy tapioca starch balls served with peanut sauce or sweet soy sauce. A beloved Sundanese street snack with an addictive, bouncy texture.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: 100 g peanuts, 5 red chilies, 2 garlic cloves, sweet soy sauce, water
instructions: Mix tapioca starch, wheat flour, garlic, and salt.
Add hot water gradually, mixing until a smooth, pliable dough forms.
Roll into small balls (1-2 cm diameter).
Boil in water until they float. Remove and drain.
Make peanut sauce: grind peanuts, chilies, and garlic. Add sweet soy sauce and water.
Serve cilok with peanut sauce and fried shallots.

title: Cireng Recipe: Fried Tapioca
description: Crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside — fried tapioca starch discs seasoned with garlic and served with spicy dipping sauce. A Sundanese snack classic.
ingredients: Spicy dip: chili, vinegar, garlic, sugar, water
instructions: Mix flours, garlic, and salt.
Add hot water gradually to form a pliable dough.
Shape into flat discs.
Deep fry in medium-hot oil until puffed and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve with spicy dipping sauce.

title: Cimol Recipe: Fried Tapioca Ball
description: Small, round tapioca starch balls that puff up when deep-fried, creating an airy, hollow center. A Sundanese snack often seasoned with spicy powder.
ingredients: Seasoning powder: chili powder, salt, garlic powder
instructions: Mix flours, garlic, and salt.
Add hot water to form a smooth dough.
Roll into small balls.
Deep fry on LOW heat — start in cool oil and gradually increase.
The balls will puff up as the oil heats.
Remove when puffed and lightly golden.
Toss with seasoning powder.

title: Combro Recipe: Fried Tempeh Ball
description: An oval-shaped fried snack with a crispy cassava exterior filled with spicy oncom (fermented soybean) filling. A Sundanese street food staple.
ingredients: Cassava dough: 300 g cassava, peeled and steamed
Filling: 200 g oncom, crumbled, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, salt
instructions: Mash steamed cassava until smooth. Season with salt.
Sauté crushed shallots, garlic, and chilies. Add crumbled oncom.
Cook filling until relatively dry.
Take a portion of cassava dough, flatten, fill with oncom mixture.
Shape into oval balls.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Serve hot.

title: Mendoan Recipe: Battered Tempeh
description: Thinly sliced tempeh dipped in a seasoned flour batter and deep-fried until just barely cooked — still soft, not crispy. A beloved Banyumas snack.
instructions: Mix flours, garlic, coriander, and water into a smooth batter.
Dip tempeh slices in batter.
Deep fry briefly until just set — the mendoan should still be soft, not crispy.
Drain briefly.
Serve immediately with sweet soy sauce.

title: Batagor Recipe: Bandung Fish Dumpling
description: Fried fish dumplings and tofu served with a rich peanut sauce. Short for 'bakso tahu goreng' — a Bandung street food icon.
ingredients: Fish paste: 300 g fish fillets, 100 g tapioca starch, 2 garlic cloves, salt
Peanut sauce: 150 g roasted peanuts, 5 red chilies, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp sweet soy sauce, water
instructions: Blend fish into a smooth paste. Mix with tapioca starch and garlic.
Stuff fish paste into tofu and wonton wrappers.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Make peanut sauce: grind peanuts, chilies, and garlic. Add sweet soy sauce and water.
Serve fried batagor with peanut sauce, lime juice, and kerupuk.

title: Siomay Recipe: Bandung Fish Dumpling
description: Steamed fish dumplings served with peanut sauce and a variety of steamed vegetables. A healthier cousin of batagor, beloved across Bandung.
ingredients: Fish paste: 400 g fish fillets, 100 g tapioca starch, 2 garlic cloves, salt, pepper
Peanut sauce: 150 g peanuts, chilies, garlic, sweet soy sauce, lime juice, water
instructions: Blend fish into a smooth paste. Mix with tapioca starch, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Place fish paste in wonton wrappers and various vegetables.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
Make peanut sauce: grind peanuts with chilies and garlic.
Add sweet soy sauce, lime juice, and water.
Serve steamed siomay with peanut sauce.

title: Lumpia Semarang Recipe: Semarang Spring Roll
description: A Semarang specialty spring roll filled with bamboo shoots, chicken, and shrimp in a savory, slightly sweet filling. Crispy outside, juicy inside.
ingredients: Filling: 200 g bamboo shoots (rebung), 100 g chicken, 50 g dried shrimp, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves
instructions: Sauté shallots and garlic. Add chicken and dried shrimp.
Add bamboo shoots and cook until tender.
Season with sweet soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Cool the filling.
Place filling on lumpia wrapper and roll tightly.
Seal edges with egg wash.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Serve with sweet chili sauce.

title: Pastel Recipe: Indonesian Curry Puff
description: A crescent-shaped pastry filled with savory curried vegetables, chicken, and egg. Crispy, flaky, and deeply satisfying — a snack found across Indonesia.
ingredients: Pastry: 300 g flour, 50 g margarine, 100 ml water, salt
Filling: 200 g diced potatoes, 100 g diced chicken, 50 g diced carrots, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp curry powder, 100 ml coconut milk
instructions: Make filling: sauté shallots and garlic. Add chicken, potatoes, carrots.
Add curry powder and coconut milk. Cook until thick.
Cool and add egg quarters.
Make pastry: mix flour, margarine, and water into a smooth dough.
Roll out, cut into circles, fill, and fold into crescents.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.

title: Risoles Recipe: Indonesian Rissole
description: Breaded and deep-fried rolls filled with ragout — a creamy mixture of minced meat, vegetables, and bechamel sauce. A colonial-era snack that has become quintessentially Indonesian.
ingredients: Crepe batter: 200 g flour, 2 eggs, 300 ml milk, salt, oil
Filling: 200 g ground chicken, 100 g diced carrots, 100 g diced potatoes, bechamel sauce (flour, butter, milk)
instructions: Make filling: cook ground chicken with vegetables. Add bechamel sauce. Cool.
Make thin crepes from batter.
Place filling on crepes and roll into cylinders.
Dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Deep fry until golden and crispy.
Serve with chili sauce.

title: Lemper Recipe: Sticky Rice Chicken Roll
description: Glutinous rice wrapped around a filling of spiced shredded chicken in coconut milk, then wrapped in banana leaf. A portable Javanese snack.
ingredients: Filling: 200 g chicken breast, shredded, cooked in spiced coconut milk
instructions: Steam glutinous rice until half-cooked.
Cook in coconut milk with pandan until fully cooked and sticky.
Cook chicken with shallots, garlic, chilies, and coconut milk. Shred.
Lay out banana leaf.
Spread sticky rice flat, place chicken filling in center.
Roll tightly in banana leaf.
Optionally, grill briefly for smoky flavor.

title: Arem-Arem Recipe: Rice Cake Roll
description: A cylindrical rice cake filled with savory spiced vegetables and sometimes meat, wrapped in banana leaf. Similar to lemper but using regular rice instead of glutinous rice.
ingredients: Filling: 200 g diced potatoes, 100 g diced carrots, 100 g tempeh, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies
instructions: Cook rice until half done.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and chilies. Add potatoes, carrots, and tempeh. Cook until done.
Lay out banana leaf.
Spread rice, add filling, roll tightly.
Steam for 20-30 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Kerak Telor Recipe: Betawi Egg Rice Crust
description: A Betawi specialty of cooked egg mixed with spiced rice, formed into a thin, crispy crust over a flame. Jakarta's most iconic street food.
instructions: Beat eggs with salt.
Mix in rice, serundeng, and dried shrimp.
Heat a small wok over medium flame.
Pour egg-rice mixture into the wok.
Cook until bottom is set and crispy.
Flip the wok upside down over the flame to crisp the top.
The kerak telor should be thin and crispy.
Drizzle with sweet soy sauce and fried shallots.

title: Kue Cubit Recipe: Mini Pancake
description: Tiny, round pancakes cooked in a special molded pan, crispy on the outside and fluffy inside. A popular Jakarta street snack often topped with chocolate sprinkles.
instructions: Mix flour, eggs, coconut milk, sugar, baking powder, and salt into a smooth batter.
Heat a kue cubit mold pan.
Pour batter into each mold.
Cook until bottoms are golden.
Add chocolate sprinkles.
Fold in half or serve as is.
Serve warm.

title: Kue Pukis Recipe: Half-Moon Cake
description: A half-moon shaped cake cooked in a special mold, with a soft, spongy texture. Popular in Java, often topped with chocolate, cheese, or coconut.
ingredients: Toppings: chocolate sprinkles, grated cheese, sweetened coconut
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, eggs, and coconut milk.
Add yeast and baking powder. Let batter rest for 30 minutes.
Heat kue pukis mold.
Pour batter into molds.
Add toppings while cooking.
Cook until golden on bottom and set on top.
Remove and serve.

title: Onde-Onde Recipe: Sesame Ball
description: Deep-fried glutinous rice flour balls coated in sesame seeds, filled with sweet mung bean paste. Crispy outside, chewy and sweet inside.
ingredients: 100 g mung beans, cooked and mashed with sugar
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, and warm water into a smooth dough.
Take a portion, flatten, and fill with mung bean paste.
Roll into a ball.
Roll in sesame seeds, pressing gently to adhere.
Deep fry on LOW heat, turning constantly.
The balls will expand as they cook.
Fry until golden and crispy.

title: Klepon Recipe: Pandan Rice Ball
description: Green glutinous rice balls filled with liquid palm sugar, rolled in grated coconut. When you bite in, the palm sugar bursts out — a delightful surprise.
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with pandan juice to form a smooth green dough.
Take a small portion, flatten, and fill with palm sugar.
Roll into a ball.
Boil in water until they float.
Remove and roll in steamed grated coconut.
Serve immediately — the palm sugar inside should still be liquid.

title: Nagasari Recipe: Banana Rice Cake
description: Slices of ripe banana wrapped in a sweet rice flour batter and steamed in banana leaves. A soft, fragrant Javanese kue with natural sweetness.
instructions: Cook rice flour, sugar, coconut milk, and salt into a thick paste.
Lay out banana leaf.
Place a spoonful of paste, add banana slice, top with more paste.
Fold banana leaf into a neat parcel.
Steam for 20-25 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Dadar Gulung Recipe: Rolled Pancake
description: Thin green pandan-flavored crepes filled with sweet grated coconut (unti). The green color comes naturally from pandan leaves.
ingredients: Crepe: 200 g flour, 2 eggs, 300 ml pandan juice, pinch of salt, oil
Filling (unti): 200 g grated coconut, 100 g palm sugar, 50 ml water, pinch of salt, pandan leaf
instructions: Make filling: cook grated coconut with palm sugar and water until dry and sweet.
Make crepe batter: mix flour, eggs, pandan juice, and salt.
Cook thin crepes in a non-stick pan.
Place filling on each crepe.
Roll into neat cylinders.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Serabi Recipe: Coconut Pancake
description: Small, round pancakes made from rice flour and coconut milk, cooked in clay pots. Crispy edges with a soft, spongy center. A traditional Javanese breakfast snack.
ingredients: Toppings: liquid palm sugar, sweet coconut sauce, or savory toppings
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, water, sugar, yeast, and salt.
Let batter rest for 1 hour until bubbly.
Heat serabi pan or small non-stick pan.
Pour a ladle of batter.
Cook until edges are crispy and center is set.
Serve with palm sugar sauce or savory toppings.

title: Bandrek Recipe: Sundanese Ginger Drink
description: A hot, warming Sundanese drink made with ginger, palm sugar, and aromatic spices. Perfect for cold mountain evenings in the Parahyangan highlands.
instructions: Crush ginger lightly.
Boil water with ginger, palm sugar, lemongrass, pandan, cloves, and cardamom.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Strain and serve hot.
Optionally add a splash of coconut milk.
A pinch of salt balances the sweetness.

title: Bajigur Recipe: Bandung Coconut Ginger
description: A sweet, warm drink from Bandung made with coconut milk, ginger, palm sugar, and pandan leaves. Creamier than bandrek due to the generous coconut milk content.
ingredients: Cooked peanuts and black glutinous rice for topping (optional)
instructions: Boil water with ginger and pandan.
Add coconut milk and palm sugar.
Heat gently — do not boil vigorously or coconut milk will separate.
Strain and serve hot.
Add peanuts or black glutinous rice for a more substantial drink.

title: Es Doger Recipe: Pink Coconut Ice
description: A vibrant pink drink of coconut milk, fermented cassava (tapai), and syrup served over shaved ice. A Sundanese refreshment with a slightly fermented tang.
instructions: Place shaved ice in a glass.
Add tapai singkong pieces.
Pour coconut milk over the ice.
Drizzle with red syrup and condensed milk.
Top with grated cheese if desired.
Serve immediately.

title: Es Selendang Mayang Recipe: Palembang Dessert
description: A colorful Palembang dessert drink with colorful jelly-like rice flour cubes in coconut milk with palm sugar syrup. The name means 'flowing scarf' in reference to the graceful colors.
ingredients: Rice flour jelly: 100 g rice flour, water, food coloring (red, green, white)
instructions: Make colored rice flour jellies: mix rice flour with water and food coloring separately.
Cook each color into a thick paste.
Press through a colander to create noodle-like shapes.
Let set.
Serve in coconut milk with palm sugar syrup over shaved ice.

title: Wedang Jahe Recipe: Javanese Ginger Tea
description: A simple, warming ginger drink sweetened with palm sugar. The Javanese word 'wedang' means hot drink, and jahe means ginger — the quintessential Javanese comfort beverage.
instructions: Crush ginger lightly to release juices.
Boil water with ginger and pandan.
Add palm sugar and stir until dissolved.
Simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Strain and serve hot.
The ginger should provide a warming, slightly spicy kick.

title: Wedang Ronde Recipe: Ginger Dumpling Drink
description: A warm ginger soup with glutinous rice dumplings filled with sweet peanut paste. The combination of spicy ginger broth and sweet dumplings is uniquely Javanese.
ingredients: Ronde: 200 g glutinous rice flour, 100 ml warm water
Filling: 100 g peanuts, 50 g palm sugar, ground together
Ginger broth: 5 cm ginger crushed, 100 g palm sugar, 1 liter water, pandan leaves, salt
instructions: Make ronde filling: grind peanuts and palm sugar.
Make dough from glutinous rice flour and warm water.
Fill dough with peanut mixture and roll into balls.
Boil ronde balls until they float.
Make ginger broth: boil ginger, palm sugar, and pandan in water.
Serve ronde in warm ginger broth.

title: Wedang Uwuh Recipe: Jogja Spice Drink
description: A traditional Yogyakarta drink made from a blend of spices including cloves, cinnamon, nutmeg leaves, and ginger, giving it a deep reddish-brown color and complex aroma.
instructions: Combine all spices in a pot with water.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Add palm sugar and stir until dissolved.
Strain and serve hot.
The drink should be deeply colored and aromatic.

title: Teh Tarik Recipe: Pulled Tea
description: Strong black tea mixed with condensed milk, then dramatically 'pulled' between two cups to create a frothy, creamy beverage. A theatrical street drink beloved across Southeast Asia.
ingredients: 2 tbsp strong black tea powder or 3 tea bags
instructions: Brew strong tea with hot water.
Add condensed milk and stir.
Pour into a tall glass.
Pour into another cup from a height — the 'pulling' action.
Repeat the pulling 3-5 times.
The tea should be frothy and well-mixed.
Serve hot or over ice.

title: Es Cincau Recipe: Grass Jelly Ice
description: Refreshing iced drink featuring cubes of dark grass jelly in sweet coconut milk with shaved ice. A cooling tropical treat popular across Indonesia.
ingredients: 200 g cincau (grass jelly), cut into cubes
100 ml simple syrup or palm sugar syrup
instructions: Cut grass jelly into small cubes.
Place in glasses over shaved ice.
Pour coconut milk over the ice.
Drizzle with sweet syrup.
Stir and enjoy.
The grass jelly has a mild, herbal flavor and satisfying jelly texture.

title: Sekoteng Recipe: Jakarta Ginger Drink
description: A traditional Betawi ginger drink with peanuts, bread cubes, and jelly in warm ginger milk. A comforting, nourishing beverage from old Jakarta.
instructions: Boil ginger in water for 10 minutes.
Add milk and sugar. Heat gently.
Serve in a bowl.
Add peanuts, bread cubes, and grass jelly.
Serve warm.

title: Es Kopyor Recipe: Young Coconut Ice
description: A refreshing drink featuring tender young coconut meat (kopyor) in sweet coconut water with shaved ice. The ultimate tropical refreshment.
ingredients: 1 young coconut, meat scraped into strips
Sweetened condensed milk or simple syrup
instructions: Scrape young coconut meat into long strips.
Place coconut meat in a glass.
Add shaved ice.
Pour coconut water over the ice.
Drizzle with condensed milk or syrup.
Add peanuts if desired.
Serve immediately.

title: Es Durian Recipe: Durian Ice
description: A decadent iced drink featuring the king of fruits — rich durian flesh blended with sweetened condensed milk and served over shaved ice. Not for the faint of heart.
instructions: Blend durian flesh with coconut milk until smooth.
Pour over shaved ice.
Drizzle generously with condensed milk.
Add sugar to taste.
Serve immediately.
Warning: the aroma is intense!

title: Susu Jahe Recipe: Ginger Milk
description: A simple, warming drink of fresh ginger steeped in hot milk with sweetener. A soothing bedtime beverage popular across Indonesia.
ingredients: 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk or sugar
instructions: Crush ginger lightly.
Heat milk with ginger over medium heat.
Steep for 5-10 minutes.
Strain out ginger.
Add sweetener and cinnamon.
Serve hot.
A calming, warming drink perfect for cold nights.

title: Bir Pletok Recipe: Betawi Spice Drink
description: A non-alcoholic Betawi drink that looks like beer but is actually a spiced drink made with ginger, lemongrass, and various spices. The foam on top gives it a beer-like appearance.
instructions: Combine all spices and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Add palm sugar until dissolved.
Strain.
Pour vigorously from a height to create foam.
Serve in tall glasses.

title: Es Gundul Recipe: Coconut Ice Drink
description: A refreshing drink of young coconut meat and coconut water served over shaved ice with sweetened condensed milk. Simple, pure coconut refreshment.
instructions: Open young coconut.
Scrape meat into strips.
Place coconut meat in a glass.
Add shaved ice.
Pour coconut water over the ice.
Drizzle with condensed milk.
Stir and enjoy.

title: Nasi Kunig Medes Recipe: Medan's Turmeric Coconut Rice
description: Aromatic turmeric rice from Medan cooked with coconut milk, lemongrass, and pandan leaves, served with various side dishes.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear
Grate fresh turmeric and squeeze to extract juice
Combine rice, coconut milk, water, turmeric juice, lemongrass, pandan leaves, bay leaves, salt and pepper in rice cooker
Cook until done and let rest for 10 minutes
Fluff with fork and remove aromatics
Serve hot with fried chicken, sambal, and emping crackers

title: Ayam Bakar Kecombrang Recipe: Torch Ginger Grilled Chicken
description: Fragrant grilled chicken marinated with kecombrang (torch ginger flower), a unique Balinese aromatic herb.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, galangal, and turmeric into smooth paste
Mix paste with sliced kecombrang, sweet soy sauce, tamarind water, and salt
Marinate chicken pieces for at least 2 hours
Grill over medium charcoal heat, basting with leftover marinade
Turn frequently until charred and cooked through
Serve with steamed rice and fresh vegetables

title: Ikan Patin Tempoyak Recipe: Catfish in Fermented Durian Sauce
description: Freshwater catfish cooked in spicy fermented durian sauce, a signature Palembang delicacy.
instructions: Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, turmeric, and shrimp paste into paste
Heat oil and sauté paste until fragrant
Add tempoyak and stir well
Pour in water and bring to simmer
Add catfish slices and cook gently for 15 minutes
Season with salt and sugar
Serve hot with steamed rice

title: Sate Babi Buleleng Recipe: Balinese Pork Satay
description: Tender pork satay from Buleleng, Bali, marinated in a rich spice paste and grilled over coconut husk charcoal.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, candlenuts, turmeric, ginger, lemongrass, coriander, and pepper
Mix spice paste with sweet soy sauce and oil
Marinate pork cubes for at least 3 hours
Thread onto bamboo skewers
Grill over hot charcoal, turning frequently
Serve with peanut sauce, rice cakes, and sambal matah

title: Tongkol Bumbu Rica Recipe: Mackerel Tuna in Manado Chili Sauce
description: Spicy grilled mackerel tuna from Manado coated in fiery rica-rica chili paste.
instructions: Grill tongkol fish until half cooked, set aside
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, and ginger into coarse paste
Heat oil and sauté paste with kaffir lime leaves
Add grilled fish and toss to coat
Season with lime juice and salt
Cook for 5 more minutes until sauce thickens
Serve with steamed rice and fresh herbs

title: Ayam Goreng Kremes Recipe: Crispy Fried Chicken with Crunchy Bits
description: Traditional Javanese fried chicken served with crispy spiced batter bits (kremes) for extra crunch.
instructions: Boil chicken in spiced coconut milk until tender
Remove chicken and let cool slightly
Mix rice flour, baking powder, coriander, turmeric, and water into thin batter
Deep fry chicken until golden and crispy
Drizzle batter into hot oil to create crispy kremes bits
Drain kremes and scatter over chicken
Serve with steamed rice and sambal

title: Babi Guling Bumbu Basa Genep Recipe: Balinese Roast Pig
description: Authentic Balinese roast pig stuffed with traditional basa genep spice paste and roasted to perfection.
instructions: Grind all spices into fine paste (basa genep)
Clean pig thoroughly and pat dry
Stuff cavity with spice paste and lemongrass stalks
Sew shut and cover with banana leaves
Roast on spit over coconut husk fire for 4-6 hours
Turn regularly until skin is crispy and golden
Carve and serve with lawar, steamed rice, and sambal

title: Becek Bumbu Merah Recipe: Duck in Red Spice Paste
description: Duck pieces braised in a vibrant red spice paste made from chilies, tomatoes, and aromatic herbs.
instructions: Boil duck pieces until half tender, drain
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, tomatoes, ginger, and shrimp paste
Heat oil and sauté paste with galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves
Add duck pieces and stir to coat
Add 1 cup water and simmer until duck is tender
Season with salt and sugar
Serve with steamed rice and vegetables

title: Sop Konro Bakso Recipe: Makassar Beef Rib Soup with Meatballs
description: Rich Makassar beef rib soup with meatballs, flavored with kluwek nut giving it a distinctive black color.
instructions: Soak kluwek nuts in hot water, extract black paste
Grind shallots, garlic, ginger, and coriander
Make bakso: mix ground beef with garlic, salt, and baking powder, form balls
Boil beef ribs with aromatics for 1.5 hours until tender
Add kluwek paste and spice paste to broth
Cook bakso balls in soup until they float
Serve with rice vermicelli, scallions, and fried shallots

title: Ikan Bakar Parape Recipe: Makassar Grilled Fish with Sour Sauce
description: Grilled fish from Makassar served with parape, a tangy and spicy sauce made from tomatoes and chili.
instructions: Score fish and rub with salt and turmeric
Grill fish on banana leaves over medium heat
For parape: blend tomatoes, chilies, shallots, and garlic coarsely
Season parape with lime juice, palm sugar, and salt
Serve grilled fish with parape sauce on top
Garnish with fresh herbs and lime wedges

title: Kambing Guling Mataram Recipe: Lombok Roast Lamb
description: Whole lamb roasted with traditional Lombok spice paste, a specialty of Mataram for special celebrations.
instructions: Grind all spices into smooth paste
Rub paste all over lamb inside and out
Let marinate for 4 hours minimum
Roast on spit over coconut husk fire
Baste with spiced coconut oil regularly
Roast for 3-4 hours until meat is tender
Carve and serve with sambal, steamed rice, and plecing kangkung

title: Ayam Bakar Manuk Lauk Recipe: Papuan Grilled Chicken
description: Traditional Papuan grilled chicken cooked with simple spices and banana leaf wrapping.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, ginger, and turmeric
Rub chicken with spice paste and salt
Wrap in banana leaves and tie with bamboo strips
Grill over medium heat for 45 minutes
Turn occasionally until cooked through
Unwrap and serve with papeda or steamed rice

title: Sapi Bumbu Bali Recipe: Balinese Spiced Beef
description: Beef chunks cooked in rich Balinese spice paste with coconut milk until tender and fragrant.
instructions: Grind all spices into smooth paste
Heat oil and sauté paste until fragrant
Add beef and brown on all sides
Pour in coconut milk and bring to simmer
Add kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass
Cook on low heat for 1.5 hours until beef is tender
Season and serve with steamed rice

title: Ikan Tuna Woku Recipe: Minahasan Tuna in Turmeric Herb Sauce
description: Fresh tuna cooked in aromatic Minahasan woku spice paste with abundant herbs and chilies.
instructions: Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, and turmeric
Heat oil and sauté paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft
Place tuna steaks in pan and spoon sauce over
Cover and cook for 10 minutes each side
Season with lime juice and salt
Serve with steamed rice and fresh vegetables

title: Bebek Bumbu Rawe Recipe: Duck in Acehnese Chili Gravy
description: Duck simmered in rich Acehnese chili gravy with spices and herbs, a fiery delicacy from Banda Aceh.
instructions: Boil duck pieces until half tender, drain and set aside
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander, and cumin
Heat oil and sauté paste with lemongrass and bay leaves
Add duck pieces and stir to coat
Add 2 cups water and tamarind water
Simmer for 45 minutes until duck is tender
Serve with steamed rice and emping crackers

title: Ayam Goreng Kalasan Premium Recipe: Yogyakarta Fried Chicken
description: Free-range chicken from Kalasan, Yogyakarta, simmered in spiced coconut milk then fried until golden.
instructions: Cut chicken into serving pieces
Simmer chicken in coconut milk with bay leaves, lemongrass, galangal, coriander, turmeric, and salt
Cook until liquid reduces and chicken is tender
Remove chicken and let cool slightly
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy
Serve with steamed rice, sambal, and fresh vegetables

title: Ikan Mujair Goreng Recipe: Crispy Fried Tilapia
description: Whole tilapia fish marinated in turmeric and coriander, deep fried until crispy and golden.
instructions: Clean and score fish
Grind turmeric, coriander, pepper, garlic, and salt into paste
Rub paste all over fish
Let marinate for 30 minutes
Deep fry in hot oil until crispy
Drain and serve with lime wedges and sambal

title: Soto Betawi Santan Recipe: Jakarta Coconut Beef Soup
description: Rich Betawi beef soup with thick coconut milk, potatoes, and aromatic spices from Jakarta.
instructions: Boil beef until tender, reserve broth
Grind shallots, garlic, and ginger
Sauté paste with galangal, lemongrass, and bay leaves
Add to beef broth with potatoes
Cook until potatoes are tender
Add coconut milk and tomatoes
Season and serve with fried shallots and scallions

title: Soto Ayam Kuah Bening Recipe: Clear Chicken Turmeric Soup
description: Clear turmeric chicken soup with vermicelli noodles, hard-boiled eggs, and fresh herbs.
instructions: Boil chicken with turmeric, lemongrass, bay leaves, shallots, garlic, and pepper
Skim foam and cook until chicken is tender
Remove chicken and shred meat
Strain broth and return to pot
Add salt to taste
Serve broth over vermicelli, bean sprouts, shredded chicken, and egg
Garnish with fried shallots, scallions, and lime

title: Sop Iler Madura Recipe: Madurese Green Bean Soup
description: Traditional Madurese soup with young cassava leaves, corn, and smoked fish in coconut broth.
instructions: Boil cassava leaves and corn in water until tender
Grind shallots, garlic, turmeric, and shrimp paste
Add spice paste to pot
Add smoked fish and coconut milk
Simmer for 15 minutes
Season with salt
Serve hot with steamed rice

title: Pindang Patik Recipe: Sour and Spicy Mackerel Soup
description: Fresh mackerel cooked in tangy tamarind broth with chilies and aromatic herbs.
instructions: Boil water with tamarind, turmeric, lemongrass, and bay leaves
Add whole mackerel fish
Add sliced chilies, shallots, and garlic
Cook for 15 minutes until fish is done
Season with salt
Serve hot with steamed rice and fresh vegetables

title: Sup Iga Panggang Recipe: Grilled Beef Rib Soup
description: Rich beef rib soup with grilled ribs that add smoky flavor, served with carrots and potatoes.
instructions: Grill beef ribs until charred on outside
Boil ribs in water with shallots, garlic, ginger, pepper, and nutmeg
Cook for 1.5 hours until tender
Add potatoes and carrots
Cook until vegetables are tender
Add tomatoes and season with salt
Serve with fried shallots and celery

title: Soto Medan Recipe: Medan Chicken Soup
description: A Medan specialty of chicken soup with a rich, yellow coconut milk broth, featuring shredded chicken, vermicelli, and hard-boiled egg.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 1 tsp coriander
Spring onions, fried shallots, lime, emping crackers
instructions: Boil chicken until tender. Shred meat. Reserve broth.
Sauté spice paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Add broth and coconut milk.
Return shredded chicken.
Cook until heated through.
Season with salt.
Serve over rice vermicelli with egg, potatoes, spring onions, fried shallots, lime, and emping.

title: Sayur Asem Sundanese Recipe: Sundanese Sour Vegetable Soup
description: Refreshing sour vegetable soup with corn, long beans, chayote, and tamarind from Sundanese cuisine.
instructions: Boil water with tamarind paste
Grind shallots, garlic, and chilies
Add ground paste to boiling water
Add peanuts and corn, cook 10 minutes
Add long beans and chayote
Cook until vegetables are tender
Season with palm sugar and salt
Serve hot with steamed rice

title: Kue Kipo Recipe: Traditional Javanese Glutinous Rice Cake
description: Small glutinous rice dumplings filled with sweet coconut, cooked in boiling water until they float.
ingredients: Filling: 150g grated coconut, 100g palm sugar, pinch of salt
instructions: Cook filling: mix grated coconut, palm sugar, and salt until dry
Mix flours with pandan water and coloring into smooth dough
Take small balls of dough, flatten and fill with coconut mixture
Seal and shape into small ovals
Boil in water until they float
Remove and serve warm

title: Lemper Ayam Recipe: Sticky Rice with Chicken Filling
description: Glutinous rice wrapped around spiced shredded chicken, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed.
instructions: Soak glutinous rice for 4 hours, drain
Steam rice with coconut milk and pandan leaves until cooked
Cook chicken with spices, shred when cool
Cut banana leaves into rectangles
Flatten rice, add chicken filling, roll and wrap
Secure with toothpicks
Steam for 15 minutes to set

title: Kue Lupis Recipe: Glutinous Rice Triangle in Palm Sugar
description: Triangular glutinous rice cakes wrapped in banana leaves, served with grated coconut and palm sugar syrup.
instructions: Cut banana leaves into strips
Fold into triangle shape and fill with rice
Wrap tightly and secure with toothpick
Boil for 2 hours until cooked through
Make palm sugar syrup: melt sugar with water and pandan
Unwrap and dip in grated coconut
Drizzle with palm sugar syrup

title: Gepuk Sapi Recipe: Sweet Smashed Beef Jerky
description: Thinly sliced beef simmered in sweet coconut milk sauce, then smashed and fried until crispy.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, galangal, ginger, and turmeric
Simmer beef slices with spice paste and coconut milk
Add lemongrass, palm sugar, pepper, and salt
Cook until liquid reduces and beef absorbs flavors
Let cool, then smash with meat mallet
Deep fry until crispy
Serve with steamed rice and sambal

title: Cireng Bumbu Rujak Recipe: Fried Tapioca with Spicy Sauce
description: Crispy fried tapioca dough served with spicy rujak sauce, a popular Sundanese snack.
ingredients: Rujak sauce: 5 red chilies, 3 shallots, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 2 tbsp tamarind water, salt
instructions: Mix tapioca flour, rice flour, garlic, and salt
Pour hot water and mix into pliable dough
Form into small flat rounds
Deep fry until puffed and crispy
For rujak sauce: grind chilies, shallots, palm sugar, tamarind, and salt
Serve cireng with rujak sauce

title: Klepon Recipe: Pandan Rice Ball
description: Green glutinous rice balls filled with liquid palm sugar, rolled in grated coconut. When you bite in, the palm sugar bursts out — a delightful surprise.
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with pandan juice to form a smooth green dough.
Take a small portion, flatten, and fill with palm sugar.
Roll into a ball.
Boil in water until they float.
Remove and roll in steamed grated coconut.
Serve immediately — the palm sugar inside should still be liquid.

title: Onde-Onde Kacang Recipe: Sesame-Coated Mung Bean Balls
description: Crispy sesame-coated balls filled with sweet mung bean paste, a popular Chinese-Indonesian snack.
instructions: Boil mung beans until soft, mash with sugar into paste
Form paste into small balls
Mix flours with warm water into dough
Flatten dough, wrap around mung bean filling
Roll in sesame seeds
Deep fry on low heat until golden and crispy
Drain and serve warm

title: Nagasari Recipe: Banana Rice Cake
description: Slices of ripe banana wrapped in a sweet rice flour batter and steamed in banana leaves. A soft, fragrant Javanese kue with natural sweetness.
instructions: Cook rice flour, sugar, coconut milk, and salt into a thick paste.
Lay out banana leaf.
Place a spoonful of paste, add banana slice, top with more paste.
Fold banana leaf into a neat parcel.
Steam for 20-25 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Bakwan Jagung Recipe: Crispy Corn Fritters
description: Crunchy fritters made from fresh corn kernels, flour, and aromatic spices, deep fried to golden perfection.
instructions: Mix corn kernels with flours, eggs, shallots, garlic, scallions, pepper, and salt
Heat oil in wok
Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil
Fry until golden brown on both sides
Drain on paper towels
Serve hot as snack or side dish

title: Savory Egg Martabak
description: Crispy, stuffed pancake filled with spiced egg and meat mixture.
ingredients: Dough: 300 g flour, 1 egg, 1 tsp salt, 150 ml water, oil
Filling: 4 eggs, 200 g minced meat, 3 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 5 green chilies, salt, pepper
Pickled cucumber and chili vinegar for serving
instructions: Make dough: mix flour, egg, salt, and water. Knead until smooth. Rest for 1 hour.
Filling: mix eggs, minced meat, chopped shallots, garlic, and chilies.
Divide dough into balls. Stretch paper-thin on an oiled surface.
Place filling in the center and fold into a square packet.
Fry in a flat pan with oil until golden and crispy on both sides.
Cut into pieces and serve with pickles.

title: Risol Bandung Recipe: Bandung-Style Crepe Rolls
description: Thin crepe rolls filled with vegetables and chicken, breaded and deep fried until crispy.
instructions: Make thin crepes and set aside
Cook filling: sauté shallots and garlic, add chicken, then vegetables
Season filling and let cool
Place filling on crepes, roll tightly
Dip in beaten egg, coat in breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden brown
Serve with chili sauce

title: Pempek Palembang Recipe: Authentic Fish Cake with Vinegar Sauce
description: The original pempek from Palembang — fish cakes made with fresh mackerel and tapioca, served with the signature dark vinegar sauce (cuko) that defines this Sumatran delicacy.
ingredients: Cuko sauce: 200 ml water, 100 g palm sugar, 50 ml vinegar, 5 red chilies, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp shrimp paste, salt
Serving: rice noodles, cucumber, fried shallots
instructions: Grind mackerel until very smooth. Mix with tapioca flour, water, salt, and sugar until a smooth, elastic dough forms.
Shape dough into various forms: long rolls (pempek lenjer), balls with egg filling (pempek telur), or flat rounds.
Boil in gently simmering water until they float and are cooked through, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove and let cool slightly. Can be served boiled or fried.
Prepare cuko: boil water with palm sugar, chilies, garlic, and shrimp paste. Add vinegar. Simmer until thick.
Serve pempek with cuko sauce, rice noodles, cucumber, and fried shallots.

title: Tahu Gejrot Recipe: Fried Tofu in Sweet Spicy Sauce
description: Crispy fried tofu pieces drenched in sweet, sour, and spicy sauce, a popular Cirebon street snack.
instructions: Fry tofu until crispy, cut into pieces
Grind chilies, shallots, and garlic coarsely
Dissolve palm sugar in water with vinegar
Add ground spices to sauce
Pour sauce over fried tofu
Serve immediately as a snack

title: Lontong Balap Recipe: Surabaya Rice Cake Salad
description: Rice cakes with bean sprouts, fried tofu, and sweet soy sauce, a signature Surabaya street food.
instructions: Cut lontong into cubes
Blanch bean sprouts briefly
Arrange lontong, sprouts, and tofu on plate
Drizzle generously with sweet soy sauce
Top with fried shallots and sambal
Serve with lime wedges

title: Kerupuk Udang Recipe: Homemade Prawn Crackers
description: Crunchy prawn crackers made from fresh shrimp and tapioca, sun-dried then deep fried.
instructions: Grind prawns with garlic until smooth
Mix with tapioca flour, salt, pepper, and water
Knead into dough
Shape into logs and wrap in banana leaves
Steam for 30 minutes
Let cool completely, refrigerate overnight
Slice thinly and sun-dry until hard
Deep fry until they puff up

title: Wedang Jahe Recipe: Javanese Ginger Tea
description: A simple, warming ginger drink sweetened with palm sugar. The Javanese word 'wedang' means hot drink, and jahe means ginger — the quintessential Javanese comfort beverage.
instructions: Crush ginger lightly to release juices.
Boil water with ginger and pandan.
Add palm sugar and stir until dissolved.
Simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Strain and serve hot.
The ginger should provide a warming, slightly spicy kick.

title: Es Kelapa Muda Sirup Recipe: Young Coconut Ice with Syrup
description: Refreshing young coconut drink with colorful syrup, a perfect tropical cooler.
instructions: Open coconuts and scoop out flesh
Pour coconut water into glass
Add coconut flesh
Drizzle with rose and simple syrup
Add ice cubes
Garnish with mint leaves

title: Jamu Kunyit Asam Recipe: Turmeric Tamarind Herbal Drink
description: Traditional Javanese herbal drink with turmeric and tamarind, known for health benefits.
instructions: Grate turmeric and squeeze to extract juice
Boil water with tamarind paste
Add turmeric juice and palm sugar
Stir until sugar dissolves
Strain and serve warm or chilled
Store in refrigerator for up to 3 days

title: Es Sinom Recipe: Young Tamarind Leaf Ice
description: Refreshing drink made from young tamarind leaves with palm sugar, a traditional Javanese cooler.
instructions: Boil tamarind leaves in water for 10 minutes
Strain and add palm sugar
Stir until sugar dissolves
Let cool completely
Serve over ice with mint garnish

title: Teh Talua Recipe: Padang Tea with Egg
description: Unique Padang beverage made with tea, egg yolk, and condensed milk, frothed until creamy.
instructions: Brew strong tea with hot water
In separate bowl, beat egg yolks with condensed milk until thick
Pour hot tea into egg mixture while stirring
Pour back and forth between two glasses to froth
Add sugar to taste
Serve hot or over ice

title: Es Rujak Buah Recipe: Fruit Salad with Spicy Palm Sugar
description: Mixed tropical fruits served with spicy palm sugar sauce, a refreshing and tangy snack.
instructions: Prepare and slice all fruits
Grind chilies coarsely
Melt palm sugar with water and tamarind
Add chilies and salt to sauce
Arrange fruits on plate
Drizzle with spicy palm sugar sauce
Serve immediately

title: Es Kepiting Recipe: Crab Ice Dessert
description: Unique Makassar dessert with crab meat, jackfruit, and coconut milk over ice.
instructions: Boil crab and extract meat
Cook palm sugar with a little water
Assemble: ice, crab meat, jackfruit
Drizzle with coconut milk and palm sugar
Add condensed milk
Serve immediately

title: Kopi Tubruk Recipe: Traditional Indonesian Coffee
description: Classic Indonesian coffee made with coarse ground coffee and hot water, served unfiltered.
instructions: Place ground coffee and sugar in glass
Pour boiling water directly over grounds
Stir briefly
Let grounds settle for 1 minute
Sip carefully from the top

title: Es Cincau Hijau Recipe: Green Grass Jelly Ice
description: Cooling drink with fresh green grass jelly, coconut milk, and palm sugar syrup.
instructions: Make palm sugar syrup: melt sugar with water and pandan
Cut grass jelly into small cubes
Fill glasses with ice and grass jelly
Pour coconut milk over
Drizzle with palm sugar syrup
Stir and serve

title: Es Sirup Malam Minggu Recipe: Saturday Night Special Ice
description: Colorful layered ice drink with various syrups, fruits, and condensed milk from Bandung.
instructions: Layer ice in tall glass
Add nata de coco and fruit cocktail
Drizzle with cocopandan and orange syrup
Pour condensed milk over the top
Top with soda water
Serve with a long spoon

title: Nasi Tempong Recipe: Spicy Banyuwangi Rice Set
description: Banyuwangi-style rice with various spicy side dishes including fried chicken, tempeh, and fiery sambal.
ingredients: Sambal tempong: 20 red chilies, 10 bird's eye chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, shrimp paste, salt
instructions: Fry chicken until crispy
Fry tempeh and tofu until golden
Stir-fry kangkung with garlic
Make sambal: grind chilies, shallots, garlic, shrimp paste, and salt
Arrange rice with all side dishes
Serve with generous sambal and fresh vegetables

title: Ayam Bakar Madu Recipe: Honey Grilled Chicken
description: Juicy grilled chicken glazed with honey and sweet soy sauce, caramelized to perfection.
instructions: Marinate chicken with honey, sweet soy sauce, lime juice, garlic, pepper, paprika, and oil
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours
Grill over medium heat, basting frequently
Turn and baste until chicken is cooked through
Serve with steamed rice and sambal

title: Ikan Bakar Bumbu Taliwang Recipe: Lombok-Style Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish coated in spicy Lombok-style chili paste, smoky and flavorful.
instructions: Score fish and rub with salt
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste into paste
Rub paste generously over fish
Wrap in banana leaves and grill
Turn once and cook until done
Serve with plecing kangkung and steamed rice

title: Bebek Bakar Bumbu Rica Recipe: Grilled Duck in Chili Sauce
description: Duck marinated in Manado rica-rica spice paste and grilled until smoky and tender.
instructions: Parboil duck pieces until half tender
Grind chilies, shallots, garlic, and ginger
Sauté paste with kaffir lime leaves
Add duck and cook in paste for 20 minutes
Grill duck pieces until charred
Serve with steamed rice and fresh vegetables

title: Grilled Oxtail Soup
description: Oxtail first grilled for smoky flavor, then simmered into rich soup.
ingredients: Ground spice paste: 8 shallots, 5 garlic cloves, 3 cm ginger, 1 tbsp coriander
instructions: Marinate oxtail in sweet soy sauce for 30 minutes.
Grill oxtail until charred on all sides.
Boil grilled oxtail in water for 2 hours until tender.
Sauté spice paste and add to broth.
Add carrots and potatoes, simmer until tender.
Season and serve with fried shallots.

title: Butter Fried Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken tossed in sweet and savory butter sauce.
ingredients: Butter sauce: 100 g butter, 3 tbsp sweet soy sauce, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tbsp lime juice
instructions: Coat chicken with flour and deep fry until crispy.
Make butter sauce: melt butter, add garlic, sweet soy sauce, pepper, and lime.
Toss fried chicken in the butter sauce.
Serve immediately with spring onions.

title: Sate Lilit Ayam Recipe: Minced Chicken Satay Balinese Style
description: Balinese-style satay made from minced chicken mixed with grated coconut and spices, wrapped around lemongrass.
instructions: Grind shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, and turmeric
Mix minced chicken with spice paste, coconut, kaffir lime leaves, coriander, and salt
Take portions and wrap around lemongrass stalks
Grill over charcoal until cooked through
Serve with steamed rice and sambal matah

title: Gulai Tambusu Recipe: Beef Intestine Curry
description: Rich Minangkabau curry made with beef intestines and offal in spiced coconut milk.
instructions: Clean and boil intestines until tender, cut into pieces
Grind shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, chilies, and coriander
Sauté paste with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves
Add intestines and stir
Pour in coconut milk and simmer
Cook until sauce thickens
Season and serve with steamed rice

title: Sumedang Fried Tofu
description: Famous West Javanese tofu — golden with light, airy texture inside.
instructions: Cut tofu into large pieces.
Soak in salt water for 15 minutes.
Drain and pat dry.
Deep fry in very hot oil until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with chili sauce.

title: Serabi Notosuman Recipe: Solo Coconut Pancake
description: Thin coconut milk pancakes from Solo, crispy on edges and soft in center, served with sweet sauce.
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, water, yeast, sugar, salt, and baking powder
Let batter rest for 1 hour
Heat clay pan and lightly oil
Pour small ladles of batter
Cook until edges are crispy and center is set
Top with coconut milk
Serve with palm sugar sauce

title: Onde-Onde Recipe: Sesame Ball
description: Deep-fried glutinous rice flour balls coated in sesame seeds, filled with sweet mung bean paste. Crispy outside, chewy and sweet inside.
ingredients: 100 g mung beans, cooked and mashed with sugar
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, and warm water into a smooth dough.
Take a portion, flatten, and fill with mung bean paste.
Roll into a ball.
Roll in sesame seeds, pressing gently to adhere.
Deep fry on LOW heat, turning constantly.
The balls will expand as they cook.
Fry until golden and crispy.

title: Getas Ketan Recipe: Fried Glutinous Rice Cake
description: Deep-fried glutinous rice cakes coated in sugar, crispy outside and chewy inside.
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with warm water and salt
Knead into smooth dough
Form into small oval shapes
Deep fry until golden
While hot, roll in sugar
Let cool and serve

title: Combro Misro Recipe: Sundanese Stuffed Cassava Balls
description: Cassava balls filled with spicy oncom (Combro) or palm sugar (Misro), deep fried until golden.
ingredients: Filling 1 (Combro): 200g oncom, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 5 red chilies, salt
instructions: Grate cassava and squeeze out excess water
For combro filling: crumble oncom, sauté with ground spices
For misro filling: use chopped palm sugar
Take cassava, flatten, fill with either filling
Shape into balls and deep fry until golden
Drain and serve

title: Pisang Molen Recipe: Banana Pastry Puffs
description: Banana pieces wrapped in flaky pastry dough and deep fried until crispy and golden.
instructions: Make dough: mix flour, margarine, egg yolk, water, and salt
Rest dough for 30 minutes
Roll out and cut into rectangles
Wrap each banana piece in dough
Seal edges with fork
Deep fry until golden brown
Drain and serve warm

title: Cucur Cake
description: Sweet disc-shaped cake with crispy edges and soft center.
instructions: Dissolve palm sugar in water. Strain.
Mix rice flour, all-purpose flour, and salt.
Add palm sugar water gradually and whisk until smooth.
Let batter rest for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a wok. Pour batter into the center.
Fry until edges are crispy and center is cooked.
Drain and serve.

title: Bakpia Pathok Recipe: Yogyakarta Mung Bean Pastry
description: Flaky pastry filled with sweet mung bean paste, a signature snack from Yogyakarta.
ingredients: Filling: 200g mung beans (boiled and mashed), 100g sugar, 2 tbsp coconut oil
instructions: Boil mung beans until soft, mash with sugar and coconut oil
Make dough: mix flour, margarine, and water
Rest dough for 30 minutes
Divide dough, flatten, wrap filling
Shape into small rounds
Bake at 180°C for 25 minutes until golden
Cool before serving

title: Putu Ayu Cake
description: Steamed cupcakes with green pandan base and white coconut topping.
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until fluffy.
Add flour, coconut milk, and baking powder.
Add pandan paste for green color.
Fill molds halfway with batter.
Top with grated coconut.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until cooked.

title: Kue Mochi Bandung Recipe: Bandung-Style Mochi
description: Soft and chewy mochi filled with peanut paste, coated in tapioca flour.
instructions: Roast and grind peanuts with sugar for filling
Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, and water
Steam batter for 20 minutes
Dust work surface with tapioca
Divide dough, flatten, add filling
Wrap and shape into balls
Dust with tapioca flour

title: Es Pisang Ior Premium Recipe: Bandung Banana Ice
description: Premium version of Bandung's es pisang ijo with matcha and red bean.
instructions: Wrap bananas in green-tinted glutinous rice batter
Steam for 15 minutes
Slice into rounds
Make matcha coconut milk: mix coconut milk with matcha
Assemble: ice, banana slices, red beans
Drizzle with matcha coconut milk and condensed milk

title: Wedang Ronde Jahe Recipe: Ginger Glutinous Rice Ball Drink
description: Warm ginger soup with chewy glutinous rice balls filled with peanut paste.
ingredients: Rice balls: 200g glutinous rice flour, 100ml warm water, food coloring
Ginger broth: 100g ginger (crushed), 100g palm sugar, 1 liter water, pandan leaves
instructions: Make filling: mix ground peanuts and sugar
Make dough: mix glutinous rice flour with warm water
Fill dough with peanut mixture, shape into balls
Cook balls in boiling water until they float
Make ginger broth: boil ginger, palm sugar, and pandan
Serve balls in warm ginger broth

title: Es Teler Durian Recipe: Durian Fruit Cocktail Ice
description: Luxurious fruit ice with durian flesh, jackfruit, coconut, and condensed milk.
instructions: Prepare all fruits
Fill glass with ice
Add durian, jackfruit, and coconut
Pour coconut milk over
Drizzle with condensed milk and palm sugar syrup
Serve immediately

title: Susu Jahe Merah Recipe: Red Ginger Milk
description: Warming milk drink infused with red ginger, palm sugar, and a hint of turmeric.
instructions: Simmer ginger in milk for 10 minutes
Add palm sugar, turmeric, and cinnamon
Strain into cups
Serve warm

title: Es Jeruk Peras Recipe: Fresh Squeezed Orange Ice
description: Fresh squeezed orange juice with ice, a refreshing Indonesian street drink.
instructions: Squeeze oranges to extract juice
Strain to remove pulp
Add sugar syrup and a pinch of salt
Serve over ice
Stir before drinking

title: Kopi Luwak Recipe: Civet Coffee Preparation
description: Premium Indonesian coffee made from civet-processed beans, known for smooth flavor.
instructions: Grind beans to medium-coarse
Place in French press or filter
Pour hot water and steep for 4 minutes
Press or filter
Add sugar if desired
Serve black for best flavor

title: Es Sop Buah Nangka Recipe: Jackfruit Fruit Soup Ice
description: Refreshing fruit soup with fresh jackfruit, melon, and coconut in sweet syrup.
instructions: Dice all fruits
Mix fruits with nata de coco
Add coconut milk and sugar
Pour over ice
Drizzle with pandan syrup
Serve chilled

title: Wedang Secang Recipe: Sappanwood Herbal Drink
description: Ruby-red herbal drink from secang wood with cinnamon and cloves, believed to have health benefits.
instructions: Boil water with secang wood, cinnamon, cloves, and pandan
Simmer for 15 minutes until deep red
Add palm sugar and stir until dissolved
Strain and serve warm or chilled

title: Ayam Goreng Menthok Recipe: Duck Fat Fried Chicken
description: Fried chicken cooked in duck fat for extra richness, a Madurese specialty.
instructions: Melt duck fat in wok
Add bay leaves, lemongrass, galangal
Add chicken pieces
Fry slowly until golden and crispy
Season with coriander, turmeric, and salt
Serve with sambal and steamed rice

title: Ikan Mujair Bakar Recipe: Charcoal-Grilled Tilapia
description: Whole tilapia marinated in turmeric and lemongrass, grilled over charcoal until smoky.
instructions: Clean and score fish
Grind turmeric, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and salt
Rub paste all over fish
Wrap in banana leaves
Grill over charcoal for 15 minutes each side
Serve with sambal and fresh vegetables

title: Sate Padang Recipe: Padang Beef Satay
description: Beef satay from Padang served with thick spicy rice flour sauce, a Minangkabau specialty.
ingredients: Rice flour batter: 3 tbsp rice flour, 500ml beef broth
Spice paste: 10 red chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves, 1 cm ginger, 1 cm galangal, 1 tsp turmeric
instructions: Boil beef until tender, reserve broth
Grill beef skewers until charred
Grind spice paste and fry in oil
Add rice flour dissolved in broth
Cook until thick, season with salt and pepper
Serve grilled satay with thick sauce over rice cakes

title: Tahu Gejrot Cirebon Recipe: Cirebon Tofu in Spicy Sauce
description: Crispy fried tofu pieces drenched in sweet and spicy tamarind sauce from Cirebon.
instructions: Fry tofu until crispy, cut into quarters
Grind chilies, shallots, and garlic coarsely
Dissolve palm sugar in water with tamarind
Add ground spices to sauce
Pour sauce over fried tofu
Serve immediately

title: Kue Cenil Recipe: Colorful Chewy Rice Cake Snack
description: Colorful chewy rice flour cakes coated in grated coconut and palm sugar.
instructions: Divide flours into portions, add different colors
Mix each with warm water into dough
Form into small logs
Boil until they float
Remove and coat in steamed grated coconut
Sprinkle with grated palm sugar
Serve as snack

title: Es Kelepon Recipe: Coconut Milk Ice with Rice Balls
description: Refreshing ice drink with colorful glutinous rice balls in coconut milk and palm sugar.
ingredients: Rice balls: 200g glutinous rice flour, pandan juice, food coloring
instructions: Make dough with glutinous rice flour and pandan juice
Fill with palm sugar cubes, shape into balls
Boil until they float
Assemble: ice, rice balls, grated coconut
Pour coconut milk over
Serve immediately

title: Intestine Satay
description: Unique Javanese satay from cleaned chicken intestines, grilled over charcoal.
ingredients: Marinade: sweet soy sauce, garlic, coriander, pepper
instructions: Clean intestines thoroughly with salt and lime.
Boil until tender, then drain.
Marinade with sweet soy sauce and spices.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal until charred.
Serve with peanut sauce and rice.

title: Nasi Empal Recipe: Sweet Fried Beef with Rice
description: Sweet and savory fried beef served with steamed rice, a Javanese specialty.
instructions: Boil beef with spices until tender
Remove and let cool slightly
Shred beef with mortar and pestle
Simmer shredded beef in coconut milk with palm sugar
Fry until crispy and caramelized
Serve with steamed rice and sambal

title: Bakso Mercon Recipe: Firecracker Meatballs
description: Extremely spicy beef meatballs stuffed with chili paste, a fiery Yogyakarta specialty.
ingredients: Filling: 20 bird's eye chilies, 5 shallots, 3 garlic cloves
instructions: Grind filling ingredients into coarse paste
Mix ground beef with tapioca, garlic, pepper, and salt
Flatten meat, add chili filling, form into balls
Boil in beef broth until they float
Serve in hot broth with fried shallots and scallions
